<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Preferred stock has a <span class="keyword">fixed dividend forever</span>, so g = 0 always.</p>
<div class="formula-box">
<span class="tex">P<sub>0</sub> = <span class="frac"><span>D</span><span>r</span></span></span>
</div>
<div class="quote mt-3 text-xs"><b>Double-Star Note:</b> Dividend is CONSTANT, g = 0, received TILL INFINITY.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Example</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Face Value = ₹100</li>
<li>• Dividend = ₹5 fixed forever</li>
<li>• Required return = 8%</li>
</ul>
<div class="calc-result mt-3"><b class="text-emerald-300">P₀ =</b> 5 / 0.08 = <span class="num">₹62.50</span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2"><b>Analogy:</b> Pay ₹62.50 once → ₹5 dividend every year forever, like a Bank FD.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Growth Rate Formula -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4"><span class="badge b-em">Growth</span><h3 class="sub-title">Sustainable Growth Rate Calculation</h3></div>
<div class="formula-box mb-4">
<span class="tex">g = ROE × Retention Ratio = ROE × (1 - Dividend Payout)</span>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Derivation</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<div><b class="text-white">Year 1:</b> Capital ₹100, ROE 20%, Payout 10%</div>
<div>Earnings = ₹20 | Div = ₹2 | Retained = ₹18</div>
<div>New Capital = ₹118</div>
<div class="mt-1"><b class="text-white">Year 2:</b> Earnings = 118 × 20% = ₹23.60</div>
<div>Growth = (23.60 − 20)/20 = <span class="num">18%</span></div>
<div class="mt-1"><b class="text-emerald-300">Formula check:</b> 20% × (1 − 0.10) = 18% ✓</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Example Problem</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Dividend Payout = 25% → Retention = 75%</li>
<li>• ROE = 21%</li>
</ul>
<div class="calc-result mt-3"><b class="text-emerald-300">g =</b> 21% × 75% = <span class="num">15.75%</span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2"><b>Key Insight:</b> More retention → more growth. 100% retention → g = ROE = 20%. Zero retention → g = 0%.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Multi-Stage DDM -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4"><span class="badge b-em">Multi-Stage</span><h3 class="sub-title">Two-Stage Dividend Discount Model</h3></div>

<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-4"><b>When to use:</b> Company growing faster than economy NOW, will slow down later. <br/><b>Examples:</b> Physics Wallah, Zomato, Eternal, new tech startups. <b>NOT</b> for: ITC, HUL (use Gordon Growth).</p>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Worked Example</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5 mb-3">
<li>• Recent dividend D₀ = ₹1</li>
<li>• Growth Years 1–2 = 15%</li>
<li>• Growth thereafter = 5% (forever)</li>
<li>• Required return r = 11%</li>
</ul>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2">Step 1 — Dividend Timeline</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Year</th><th>Calc</th><th>D</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>1</td><td>1 × 1.15</td><td>1.15</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>1.15 × 1.15</td><td>1.3225</td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>1.3225 × 1.05</td><td>1.3886</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2">Step 2 — Terminal Value @ Y2</div>
<div class="formula-box text-xs">
<span class="tex">P<sub>2</sub> = <span class="frac"><span>D<sub>3</sub></span><span>r-g</span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>1.3886</span><span>0.06</span></span> = 23.1438</span>
</div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2 mt-3">Step 3 — Cash Flows</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Y1: 1.15 | Y2: 1.3225 + 23.1438 = 24.4663</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-1 mt-3">Step 4 — Discount to Today</div>
<div class="formula-box text-xs">
<span class="tex">P<sub>0</sub> = <span class="frac"><span>1.15</span><span>1.11</span></span> + <span class="frac"><span>24.4663</span><span>1.2321</span></span> = 1.0360 + 19.8574</span>
</div>
<div class="calc-result mt-3 text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">P₀ =</b> <span class="num text-lg">₹20.89</span></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Deferred Dividend -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4"><span class="badge b-em">Special</span><h3 class="sub-title">Deferred Dividend Problem</h3></div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Setup</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li>• NO dividend for first 3 years</li>
<li>• First dividend at END of Year 4</li>
<li>• Earnings Y4 = ₹1.64, Payout = 50%</li>
<li>• Constant growth after = 5%</li>
<li>• Required return = 10%</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Solution</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<div><b>Step 1:</b> D₄ = 1.64 × 50% = ₹0.82</div>
<div><b>Step 2:</b> Value at Y3 = D₄/(r−g) = 0.82/0.05 = ₹16.40</div>
<div><b>Step 3:</b> Discount Y3 → today</div>
<div class="font-mono">P₀ = 16.40 / (1.10)³ = 16.40/1.331</div>
</div>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">P₀ =</b> <span class="num">₹12.32</span></div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="quote mt-3 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Key Rule:</b> If first dividend is at Year n → Terminal value is at Year (n−1), then discount back to Year 0.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Model Selection Decision Tree -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-4">When to Use Which Valuation Model?</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">MATURE & STABLE</div>
<div class="text-sm text-white font-bold mb-2">Single-Stage Gordon</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-400 space-y-1">
<li>• ITC, HUL (Unilever)</li>
<li>• Infosys, PFC, REC</li>
<li>• Constant growth, dividend payers</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">NEW & HIGH-GROWTH</div>
<div class="text-sm text-white font-bold mb-2">Multi-Stage DDM / FCFE</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-400 space-y-1">
<li>• Physics Wallah, Zomato</li>
<li>• Eternal, new tech startups</li>
<li>• High growth → stable</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">PREFERRED STOCK</div>
<div class="text-sm text-white font-bold mb-2">P₀ = D / r</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-400 space-y-1">
<li>• Fixed dividend forever</li>
<li>• g = 0</li>
<li>• Bank FD analogy</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mt-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-3">Common Mistakes to Avoid</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Mistake</th><th class="text-emerald-300">Correction</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Using D₀ instead of D₁</td><td>Always use NEXT period's dividend in numerator</td></tr>
<tr><td>Forgetting r &gt; g condition</td><td>If r ≤ g, Gordon Growth is INVALID</td></tr>
<tr><td>Wrong timing of terminal value</td><td>First div at Year n → Value at Year (n−1)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Multi-stage for young companies skipped</td><td>Young companies NEED multi-stage</td></tr>
<tr><td>DDM for non-dividend payers</td><td>Use FCFE for Reliance, Zomato</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch4" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">04</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 4 · Multiples</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Relative Valuation & EV/EBITDA</h2>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Method of Comparable -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4"><span class="badge b-em">Approach 1</span><h3 class="sub-title">Method of Comparable (Comparable Company Analysis)</h3></div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Compare two or more similar stocks to determine which is undervalued (BUY) or overvalued (DO NOT BUY).</p>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Property Analogy</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Property A: ₹1,00,000/sq.yd | Property B: ₹1,20,000/sq.yd</li>
<li>• Average rate = ₹1,10,000/sq.yd</li>
<li>• A &lt; Avg → CHEAPER → BUY | B &gt; Avg → EXPENSIVE → DO NOT BUY</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-2">⚠ Important Caution</div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-2">A cheap multiple ≠ blind BUY. Understand WHY it's cheap.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-rose-300"><b>IndusInd Bank:</b> Low PE (10x) BUT governance issues, earnings manipulation → DO NOT BUY</div>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-1"><b>HDFC Bank:</b> Cheap PE + quality + good governance → BUY</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Location Matters Analogy</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Connaught Place: ₹5L/sq.yd (Prime)<br/>Seemapuri: ₹10K/sq.yd (Slum)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">Cheap ≠ better. A stock may be cheap for valid reasons (poor management, declining business, regulatory issues).</div>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">PE Ratio — Logic and Calculation</h4>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Understanding PE Logically</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Bank FD: Deposit ₹100 → ₹107 after 1 year (7% interest).</p>
<div class="formula-box text-xs">
<span class="tex">PE of FD = <span class="frac"><span>100</span><span>7</span></span> = 14.28</span>
</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">To earn ₹1 from FD → invest ₹14.28. Quality stock at PE ~14–15 = GOOD VALUE. PE 60–70 = TOO HIGH.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">HDFC vs ICICI Decision</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th></th><th>HDFC Bank</th><th>ICICI Bank</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Price</td><td>₹750.40</td><td>₹1,259.20</td></tr>
<tr><td>EPS</td><td>₹49.28</td><td>₹74.77</td></tr>
<tr><td>PE</td><td><span class="num">15.22</span></td><td><span class="num">16.84</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-2">Avg PE = (15.22+16.84)/2 = <span class="num">16.03</span></div>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Decision:</b> HDFC PE (15.22) &lt; Avg → BUY HDFC ✓ <br/>ICICI PE (16.84) &gt; Avg → DO NOT BUY</div>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Other Multiples (When Earnings Negative)</h4>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-1">Problem with PE</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Physics Wallah: Price ₹100, Earnings −₹1 → PE = −100 (MEANINGLESS)</div>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">Alternative Multiples</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li>• <b>Price/Sales (P/S)</b></li>
<li>• <b>Price/Book Value (P/BV)</b></li>
<li>• <b>Price/Cash Flow (P/CF)</b></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">PW: P/S = 6.77 → ₹6.77 for every ₹1 of sales</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Method of Fundamental -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4"><span class="badge b-em">Approach 2</span><h3 class="sub-title">Method of Fundamental (Fundamental PE)</h3></div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Tells what PE a stock SHOULD trade at (Fair Value PE). Derived from Gordon Growth.</p>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Derivation</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">From Gordon: $P_0 = \frac{D_1}{r-g}$. Divide both sides by E₁:</div>
<div class="formula-box mt-2">
<span class="tex"><span class="frac"><span>P<sub>0</sub></span><span>E<sub>1</sub></span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>DPR</span><span>r - g</span></span></span>
</div>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Leading (Forward) PE</div>
<div class="formula-box text-xs"><span class="tex"><span class="frac"><span>P<sub>0</sub></span><span>E<sub>1</sub></span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>DPR</span><span>r - g</span></span></span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">E₁ = next year's earnings</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Trailing (Current) PE</div>
<div class="formula-box text-xs"><span class="tex"><span class="frac"><span>P<sub>0</sub></span><span>E<sub>0</sub></span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>DPR × (1+g)</span><span>r - g</span></span></span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">E₀ = current reported earnings</div>
</div>
</div>

<table class="pretty mb-4">
<thead><tr><th>Condition</th><th>Interpretation</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Fundamental PE &gt; Market PE</td><td>Stock UNDERVALUED</td><td><span class="hl">BUY</span></td></tr>
<tr><td>Fundamental PE &lt; Market PE</td><td>Stock OVERVALUED</td><td><span class="danger">DO NOT BUY</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Example 1</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5 mb-2"><li>• DPR = 30%, R = 13%, G = 6%</li></ul>
<div class="formula-box text-xs"><span class="tex"><span class="frac"><span>0.30</span><span>0.13 - 0.06</span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>0.30</span><span>0.07</span></span> = 4.28</span></div>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Fundamental PE =</b> <span class="num">4.28x</span></div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Example 2</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5 mb-2"><li>• DPR = 60%, R = 15%, G = 7%</li></ul>
<div class="formula-box text-xs"><span class="tex"><span class="frac"><span>0.60</span><span>0.15 - 0.07</span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>0.60</span><span>0.08</span></span> = 7.5</span></div>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Fundamental PE =</b> <span class="num">7.5x</span></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- EV/EBITDA -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4"><span class="badge b-em">Multiple</span><h3 class="sub-title">EV/EBITDA Multiple</h3></div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3"><b>When to use:</b> Extensively used for <span class="keyword">MANUFACTURING companies</span> (Dabur, HUL).</p>

<div class="formula-box mb-4">
<span class="tex"><span class="frac"><span>EV</span><span>EBITDA</span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>Enterprise Value</span><span>EBITDA</span></span></span>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">EBITDA</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation & Amortization. Think: <span class="keyword">cash profits</span>.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Enterprise Value (EV)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Price the market is willing to pay for ALL assets. If you sold ALL assets today, what would you get?</p>
<p class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-2 font-semibold">⚠ EV ≠ Net Worth!</p>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">House Analogy — EV vs Net Worth</h4>
<table class="pretty mb-4">
<thead><tr><th>Case</th><th>House <span class="text-cyan-300">(= EV)</span></th><th>Loan</th><th>Cash</th><th class="text-cyan-300">EV</th><th class="text-emerald-300">Net Worth</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>A</td><td>₹3 Cr</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>₹3 Cr</td><td>₹3 Cr</td></tr>
<tr><td>B</td><td>₹3 Cr</td><td>₹1 Cr</td><td>0</td><td>₹3 Cr</td><td>₹2 Cr</td></tr>
<tr><td>C</td><td>₹3 Cr</td><td>₹1 Cr</td><td>₹50 L</td><td>₹3 Cr</td><td>₹2.5 Cr</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div class="formula-box mb-4">
<span class="tex">EV = Market Value of Equity + Market Value of Debt - Cash &amp; Investments</span>
<span class="tex">Equity Value = EV - Debt + Cash &amp; Investments</span>
</div>

<!-- HUL Example -->
<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Real Example — Hindustan Unilever (HUL) Valuation</h4>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-4">
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Step 1 — Lowest EV/EBITDA (5 yrs)</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Year</th><th>EV/EBITDA</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>1</td><td>35x</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>38x</td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>34x</td></tr>
<tr><td>4</td><td>33x</td></tr>
<tr><td>5</td><td class="text-emerald-300 font-bold">31.88x ← LOWEST</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">Conservative approach</div>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Step 2–5 — Calculation</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1.5">
<li><b>EBITDA:</b> ₹1,45,540 lakhs</li>
<li><b>EV:</b> 31.88 × 1,45,540 = ₹46,39,815.2 lakhs</li>
<li><b>− Total Debt:</b> ₹14,780 lakhs</li>
<li><b>+ Cash & STI:</b> ₹69,930 lakhs</li>
<li><b>= Equity Value:</b> ₹46,94,965.2 lakhs</li>
<li><b>Shares Outstanding:</b> 2,349.6 million (234.96 Cr)</li>
<li class="calc-result text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Value per Share =</b> <span class="num">₹1,998 ≈ ₹2,000</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="quote mt-3 text-xs"><b>Conclusion:</b> Fair Value HUL ≈ ₹2,000. CMP ≈ ₹2,100. If HUL falls to ₹2,000 → AGGRESSIVELY BUY. Historical movement: ₹2,376 → ₹2,050 (US-Iran tensions) → ₹1,550.</div>
</div>

<!-- EV/EBITDA detailed example -->
<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">EV/EBITDA — Detailed Calculation Example</h4>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Given Data</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li>• Number of shares = 2,00,000</li>
<li>• Price per share = ₹40</li>
<li>• Long-term Debt (Book) = ₹9,00,000</li>
<li>• Long-term Debt (Market) = ₹6,00,000</li>
<li>• Short-term Debt (Book) = ₹12,00,000</li>
<li>• Cash = ₹2,50,000</li>
<li>• EBITDA = ₹1,00,000</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Solution</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li><b>MV Equity:</b> 2,00,000 × 40 = ₹80,00,000</li>
<li><b>MV Debt:</b> 6,00,000 + 12,00,000 = ₹18,00,000</li>
<li class="text-slate-400">(ST Debt: book ≈ market)</li>
<li><b>EV:</b> 80L + 18L − 2.5L = ₹95,50,000</li>
</ul>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">EV/EBITDA =</b> 95,50,000 / 1,00,000 = <span class="num">9.55</span></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch5" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">05</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 5 · Asset-Based</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Net Asset Value (NAV) Method</h2>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">NAV is the price you should pay for a company based on its assets, not its earnings power.</p>
<div class="formula-box mb-4">
<span class="tex">NAV = Fair Value of Assets - Liabilities</span>
<span class="tex">NAV per Share = <span class="frac"><span>NAV</span><span>Number of Shares</span></span></span>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">✓ WHEN to Use NAV</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li class="check-li"><span>Company in <b>FINANCIAL DISTRESS</b></span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>You care about <b>ASSETS</b>, not earnings</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Asset values are <b>STABLE</b></span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Examples: Jet Airways (aircraft), Reliance Communications (spectrum)</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">✗ WHEN NOT to Use NAV</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li class="x-li"><span><b>HYPERINFLATION</b> (inflation &gt; 100% over 3 yrs)</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Companies with mostly <b>INTANGIBLE</b> assets (software)</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Healthy growing companies (Reliance won't sell at NAV)</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">NAV Calculation — Worked Example</h4>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mb-3"><b>Given:</b> 2,000 shares. Fixed Assets MV = 120% of BV. All other items: MV = BV.</div>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">ASSETS (Fair Value)</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Item</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Cash</td><td>₹10,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>Accounts Receivable</td><td>₹20,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>Inventory</td><td>₹500</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed Assets (₹1,20,000 × 1.20)</td><td>₹1,44,000</td></tr>
<tr><td class="font-bold">Total Assets</td><td class="font-bold text-emerald-300">₹1,74,500</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">LIABILITIES</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Item</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Accounts Payable</td><td>₹5,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>Notes (Short-term)</td><td>₹30,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>Term Loan</td><td>₹45,000</td></tr>
<tr><td class="font-bold">Total Liabilities</td><td class="font-bold text-rose-300">₹80,000</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="calc-result mt-4">
<div class="text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">NAV =</b> 1,74,500 − 80,000 = <span class="num">₹94,500</span></div>
<div class="text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">NAV per Share =</b> 94,500 / 2,000 = <span class="num text-lg">₹47.25</span></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Method Selection Table -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Master Decision Table — When to Use Which Method</h3>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Method</th><th class="text-emerald-300">When to Use</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">DDM</b></td><td>Dividend-paying companies, stable growth (ITC, Infosys)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">DCF / FCFE</b></td><td>No comparable companies; non-dividend payers (Reliance, Zomato)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Relative — Comparable</b></td><td>Comparable companies available (HDFC vs ICICI)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Relative — Fundamental</b></td><td>Determine fair PE from fundamentals</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">EV/EBITDA</b></td><td>Manufacturing companies (HUL, Dabur)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">NAV</b></td><td>Financially distressed; asset-heavy companies</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<!-- Adv/Disadvantages -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-4">Advantages & Disadvantages of All Methods</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2">DDM</div>
<div class="text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-400">+ Advantages:</b></div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5 mb-2">
<li class="check-li"><span>Easy to compute</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Simple formula</span></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs"><b class="text-rose-400">− Disadvantages:</b></div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li class="x-li"><span>Sensitive to G, R inputs</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Assumes dividends continue forever</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Small Δ in g/r → large Δ valuation</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-cyan-300 mb-2">Relative Valuation</div>
<div class="text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-400">+ Advantages:</b></div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5 mb-2">
<li class="check-li"><span>Easy to compute</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Simple comparison</span></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs"><b class="text-rose-400">− Disadvantages:</b></div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li class="x-li"><span>Sensitive to multiple chosen</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Comparables may not exist (Reliance, ITC, PW)</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Multiple answers possible (PE→HDFC, P/BV→ICICI)</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-violet-300 mb-2">NAV</div>
<div class="text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-400">+ Advantages:</b></div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5 mb-2">
<li class="check-li"><span>Provides FLOOR VALUE (min)</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Tells minimum price to pay</span></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs"><b class="text-rose-400">− Disadvantages:</b></div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li class="x-li"><span>Only for distressed companies</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>NOT during hyperinflation</span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span>Not for intangible-asset companies</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch6" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">06</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 6 · Market Behavior</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Market Efficiency & Behavioral Finance</h2>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Meaning of Market Efficiency -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Meaning of Market Efficiency</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Stock prices REFLECT all available information. NO mispricing — prices fully, quickly, rationally reflect data.</p>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-2">⚠ Common Trap</div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300">"If market is efficient, making money is easy."</p>
<div class="text-sm text-rose-300 font-bold mt-2">❌ WRONG.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">✓ Correct Answer</div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300">Efficient market → No undervalued stocks → Making money is <span class="danger">VERY DIFFICULT</span>.</p>
<div class="text-sm text-emerald-300 font-bold mt-2">→ Invest PASSIVELY (not actively)</div>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Active vs Passive Investing</h4>
<table class="pretty mb-3">
<thead><tr><th>Approach</th><th class="text-cyan-300">Active</th><th class="text-emerald-300">Passive</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Approach</td><td>Use brain to pick stocks</td><td>Replicate index without thinking</td></tr>
<tr><td>Research</td><td>Individual stock research</td><td>Copy index weights (HDFC 10%, Reliance 8%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Goal</td><td>Beat the market</td><td>Match the market</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="quote text-xs">More efficient markets → No mispricing → Manage money PASSIVELY rather than ACTIVELY.</div>
</div>

<!-- Market vs Intrinsic Value -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Market Value vs Intrinsic (Fundamental) Value</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">MARKET VALUE</div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300">Price at which you can BUY or SELL today. Reliance @ ₹1,300.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-1">INTRINSIC VALUE</div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300">Analyst's calculated value — <span class="keyword">person-specific</span>.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">Jefferies says ₹1,500 | JP Morgan says ₹1,200 — different analysts, different intrinsic values.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Factors Promoting Efficiency -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Six Factors Promoting Market Efficiency</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">1</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Large Number of Participants</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">More buyers/sellers → better price discovery</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">2</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Greater Data Availability</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Better info flow → faster price reflection</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">3</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Lower Transaction Costs</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">High costs discourage trading</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">4</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Foreign Investors Allowed</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">More capital → better discovery</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">5</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Short Selling Allowed</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Corrects overvalued stocks</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">6</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Restrictions on Insider Trading</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">⭐ Only good restriction. Mukesh Ambani can't trade Reliance</div></div></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Forms of Market Efficiency -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Four Forms of Market Efficiency (Master Table)</h3>
<div class="quote text-xs mb-3"><b>Important Rule:</b> As efficiency ↑ → Making money becomes more difficult. Shift from ACTIVE to PASSIVE.</div>

<table class="pretty mb-4">
<thead><tr><th>Form</th><th>Prices Reflect</th><th>What Works?</th><th>Strategy</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><b class="text-rose-300">Weak-Form INEFFICIENT</b></td>
<td>NOTHING</td>
<td>Technical ✓ Fundamental ✓ Insider ✓ — ALL work</td>
<td><span class="hl">ACTIVE</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><b class="text-amber-300">Weak-Form EFFICIENT</b><div class="text-[10px] text-slate-500">(= Semi-Strong Inefficient)</div></td>
<td>Market Data only<br/>(Price + Volume)</td>
<td>Technical ✗ | Fundamental ✓ Insider ✓</td>
<td><span class="hl">ACTIVE</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><b class="text-cyan-300">Semi-Strong EFFICIENT</b><div class="text-[10px] text-slate-500">(= Strong-Form Inefficient)</div></td>
<td>ALL Public Data</td>
<td>Technical ✗ Fundamental ✗ | ONLY Insider ✓</td>
<td><span class="hl">PASSIVE</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><b class="text-emerald-300">Strong-Form EFFICIENT</b></td>
<td>ALL Public + ALL Private</td>
<td>NOTHING works (Technical ✗ Fundamental ✗ Insider ✗)</td>
<td><span class="hl">PASSIVE</span></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Exam Question Patterns</h4>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Q-Type 1</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">"Made money using TECHNICAL ANALYSIS"</p>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 font-bold">→ Weak-Form INEFFICIENT</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Q-Type 2</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">"FUNDAMENTAL ANALYST"</p>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 font-bold">→ Weak-Form EFFICIENT (more correct)</div>
<div class="text-[10px] text-slate-400 mt-1">Virat &gt; Rohit is more accurate than Virat &gt; Vikas</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Q-Type 3</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">"INSIDER TRADING worked"</p>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 font-bold">→ Semi-Strong EFFICIENT</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-3">Three Analysis Types Explained</div>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-3">
<div>
<b class="text-white text-sm">Technical Analysis</b>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Charts, candlestick patterns, support/resistance. Short-term traders. Also for commodities like Gold.</p>
</div>
<div>
<b class="text-white text-sm">Fundamental Analysis</b>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Research competitors, profitability, industry. Long-term capital appreciation, buy & hold.</p>
</div>
<div>
<b class="text-white text-sm">Insider Trading</b>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1"><span class="warning">ILLEGAL in India.</span> CEO/auditors trading on non-public info. Banned for Ambani, HDFC auditors (EY).</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Anomalies -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Anomalies in Market Efficiency</h3>
<div class="quote text-xs mb-4"><b>Important:</b> Anomalies are NOT violations of market efficiency. They result from <span class="warning">POOR RESEARCH METHODOLOGY</span>. Like saying "Vaibhav Suryavanshi scored most runs THIS IPL" doesn't mean he's the best of ALL IPLs.</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">1. January Effect (US) / April Effect (India)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Markets fall Dec, rise Jan. Two reasons:</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">
<b class="text-emerald-300">A. Tax Loss Harvesting:</b><br/>
<span class="text-slate-400">₹1 Cr profit, 10% tax = ₹10 L owed. ₹90 L unrealized loss in Reliance → Sell in Dec, book loss → Net profit ₹10 L → Tax ₹1 L (saved ₹9 L). Buy back in Jan.</span>
</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-2">
<b class="text-emerald-300">B. Window Dressing:</b><br/>
<span class="text-slate-400">Fund managers sell controversial stocks (Vodafone) before reporting period → Buy back in Jan.</span>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2. Momentum vs Overreaction Effect</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2"><b class="text-emerald-300">Momentum:</b> "Stock rose 40x, will keep rising" → BUY using charts</p>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2"><b class="text-rose-300">Overreaction:</b> "Rose too much, will fall now" → SELL using charts</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Both use TECHNICAL → assume Weak-Form Inefficient.<br/><b>Example:</b> SSSC $41 → $600 in 1 year.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">3. Size Effect</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Small-caps OUTPERFORM large-caps.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">HDFC Bank (Large) ← struggles to grow 40%<br/>AU Small Bank ← can grow 40–50%</div>
<div class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-2"><b>⚠ Caveat:</b> Small-caps carry MORE RISK. Risk-adjusted returns may NOT beat large-caps.</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Assumes Weak-Form Inefficient / Semi-Strong Inefficient.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">4. Value vs Growth Stocks</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b class="text-emerald-300">Value:</b> Cheap valuations (HDFC PE 15)</p>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2"><b class="text-cyan-300">Growth:</b> Expensive (NVIDIA PE 57)</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Buffett belief: Value &gt; Growth. Requires <b>Fundamental Analysis</b> → Assumes Weak-Form Efficient / Semi-Strong Inefficient.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">5. IPOs are Undervalued</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Popular belief: "IPOs give quick money."</p>
<div class="text-xs text-rose-300 mt-2"><b>REALITY:</b> Majority of IPOs do NOT perform well. Belief is generally WRONG.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">6. ETFs Should Trade at NAV</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">ETF should = iNAV (Indicative NAV).</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1"><b>SBI Nifty 50 ETF:</b> iNAV ₹250.61 vs Price ₹250.42 (diff ₹0.19).</div>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-1">Difference NOT significant enough to exploit.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Behavioral Finance -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Behavioral Finance — Investor Behaviors</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-400 mb-4">Studies how investors behave — RATIONALLY or IRRATIONALLY?</p>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1"><span class="lucide">👥</span><b class="text-white">1. Herding & Information Cascade</b></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">Other investors MIMIC big/informed investor's decisions.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1"><b>Example:</b> "Rakesh Jhunjhunwala bought Tata Motors" → many follow.</div>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-2">✓ Makes market MORE efficient (informed investor's research spreads → price corrects).</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1"><span class="lucide">📉</span><b class="text-white">2. Loss Aversion</b></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">People DISLIKE losses MORE than they LIKE equivalent gains.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Finding ₹500 (happy) vs Losing ₹500 (very sad — bigger emotion).</div>
<div class="text-xs text-rose-300 mt-2">During COVID: rational = BUY (cheap stocks); actual = SOLD (panic).</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1"><span class="lucide">🔁</span><b class="text-white">3. Representativeness</b></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">Assuming the past will REPEAT in the future.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">"Gold rose 40 yrs → will keep rising" / "Property never gave losses."</div>
<div class="text-xs text-rose-300 mt-2">Past ≠ guarantee of future.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1"><span class="lucide">🖼️</span><b class="text-white">4. Narrow Framing</b></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">Looking at things from a very NARROW perspective.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1"><b>Example:</b> "US-Iran war → why India falls?" Missing: Iran oil → ↑ oil prices → ↑ India inflation.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1"><span class="lucide">⚓</span><b class="text-white">5. Disposition Effect</b></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">AVOID realizing losses. Hold losers too long.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Holding ₹2 Cr loss positions, hoping for recovery.</div>
<div class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-2"><b>vs Loss Aversion:</b> LA panics & books losses too fast. DE holds & never books.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-1"><span class="lucide">🐌</span><b class="text-white">6. Overconfidence & Conservatism</b></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">SLOW to react to new data.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1"><b>Conservatism:</b> "HDFC won't fall" despite governance issues.</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400"><b>Overconfidence:</b> Hold NVIDIA despite negative news.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- MCQs -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Key MCQ Solutions</h3>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2" open>
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q1: Informationally efficient market means...</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs space-y-1">
<div class="text-rose-300">(a) Active fund managers earn abnormal returns ✗</div>
<div class="text-emerald-300">(b) Security prices reflect new data quickly ✓ — DEFINITION</div>
<div class="text-rose-300">(c) Investors react to ALL data ✗ (they react to NEW data)</div>
</div>
</details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2">
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q2: Meaning of Intrinsic Value</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs space-y-1">
<div class="text-emerald-300">(a) Changes through time as new data is released ✓</div>
<div class="text-rose-300">(b) Price for buying/selling ✗ (that's market value)</div>
<div class="text-rose-300">(c) Easily determined by calculator ✗ (requires research)</div>
</div>
</details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2">
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q3: Short Selling and Market Efficiency</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs text-emerald-300">Short selling PROMOTES market efficiency. Allows correction of overvalued stocks. Should be ALLOWED.</div>
</details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2">
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q4: Weak-Form Efficient market reflects what?</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs text-emerald-300">Only MARKET DATA (Price + Volume).</div>
</details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2">
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q5: Performance of money managers tends to be...</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">
<b class="text-emerald-300">INFERIOR</b> on risk-adjusted basis. Even if 17% vs Nifty 12%, must check RISK. Analogy: Person A drives 100 km/h fast; Person B drives 60 km/h safe — risk-adjusted, B may be better.
</div>
</details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2">
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q6: With respect to anomalies...</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs text-emerald-300">Reported anomalies are NOT violations. They result from POOR RESEARCH METHODOLOGY.</div>
</details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2">
<summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q7: Meaning of Loss Aversion</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary>
<div class="mt-3 text-xs text-emerald-300">We dislike losses MORE than we like comparable gains.</div>
</details>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch7" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">07</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 7 · Indexes</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Security Market Indexes</h2>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Intro to Indexes -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">What Are Indexes?</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Indexes represent <span class="keyword">PERFORMANCE</span> — they tell us how a market, asset class, or segment is performing.</p>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">1. Asset Class Performance</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">How much did EQUITY, REAL ESTATE, COMMODITIES earn?</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2. Security Market (Broader)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Overall stock market: NIFTY 50, SENSEX 30, S&P 500</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">3. Segment / Sector</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">NIFTY BANK, NIFTY IT, NIFTY AUTO</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-2">Cricket Team Analogy</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">India = 100+ Crore people. World Cup team = 11 players representing entire country.<br/>NSE has 2,400+ stocks. NIFTY 50 has 50 stocks representing the market.</p>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2"><b class="text-emerald-300">Constituents</b> = individual stocks in an index. <b class="text-emerald-300">Reconstitution</b> = changing constituents.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">
<b>Examples of Past Reconstitution:</b><br/>
• Yes Bank, Indiabulls Housing Finance — REMOVED (poor performance/scandals)<br/>
• Adani Enterprises, Zomato — ADDED (good performance)
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Two Types of Returns -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Two Types of Returns</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">PRICE RETURN</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Only PRICE movement (capital appreciation). NO dividends.</p>
<div class="formula-box text-xs"><span class="tex">Price Return = <span class="frac"><span>P<sub>1</sub> - P<sub>0</sub></span><span>P<sub>0</sub></span></span></span></div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">TOTAL RETURN</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Includes BOTH price AND dividends. Always ≥ Price Return.</p>
<div class="formula-box text-xs"><span class="tex">Total Return = <span class="frac"><span>P<sub>1</sub> + D - P<sub>0</sub></span><span>P<sub>0</sub></span></span></span></div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">Example</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Stock bought ₹100, became ₹110, gave ₹2 dividend.</p>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Price Return:</b> (110−100)/100 = <span class="num">10%</span> | <b>Total Return:</b> (110+2−100)/100 = <span class="num">12%</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Five Weight Systems -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-4">Five Weight Systems (Most Important Topic)</h3>

<div data-xdata="{tab: 'price'}">
<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2 mb-4">
<button data-xclick="tab='price'" data-xclass="tab==='price'?'active':''" class="tab-btn">1. Price Weighted</button>
<button data-xclick="tab='equal'" data-xclass="tab==='equal'?'active':''" class="tab-btn">2. Equal Weighted</button>
<button data-xclick="tab='mcap'" data-xclass="tab==='mcap'?'active':''" class="tab-btn">3. Market Cap</button>
<button data-xclick="tab='float'" data-xclass="tab==='float'?'active':''" class="tab-btn">4. Free Float Mkt Cap</button>
<button data-xclick="tab='fund'" data-xclass="tab==='fund'?'active':''" class="tab-btn">5. Fundamental</button>
</div>

<!-- Price Weighted -->
<div data-xshow="tab==='price'" class="glass-2 p-5">
<h4 class="font-bold text-white mb-2">1. Price Weighted</h4>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Buy ONE share of EACH stock. Higher price stock gets more weight automatically.</p>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mb-3 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs text-amber-300"><b>⚠ KEY POINT:</b> Company size is NOT determined by stock price!</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-2">MRF @ ₹1,22,000 (smaller) vs Reliance @ ₹1,200 (much bigger — ~₹20 L Cr MCap).</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Reliance issued MANY shares; MRF issued FEW. Size = Market Cap, not price.</div>
</div>
<table class="pretty mb-3">
<thead><tr><th>Stock</th><th>P₀</th><th>P₁</th><th>Div</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>A</td><td>₹100</td><td>₹110</td><td>₹1</td></tr><tr><td>B</td><td>₹50</td><td>₹52</td><td>₹1</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 text-xs">
<div class="glass-2 p-3"><b class="text-cyan-300">Price Return:</b><br/>P₀ Portfolio = 100+50 = ₹150<br/>P₁ Portfolio = 110+52 = ₹162<br/>Return = (162−150)/150 = <span class="num">8%</span></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-3"><b class="text-emerald-300">Total Return:</b><br/>P₁+Div = 110+1+52+1 = ₹164<br/>Return = (164−150)/150 = <span class="num">9.33%</span></div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">⭐ KEY CHARACTERISTIC: Divisor Adjustment for Stock Split</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Stocks: 10, 20, 60 → Avg = 30. Stock C 3-for-1 split → 10, 20, 20. New Divisor = 50/30 = <span class="num">1.667</span>.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2"><b>MCQ:</b> P₁ = 12, 19, 22 → Index = (12+19+22)/1.667 = 53/1.667 = <span class="num">31.79</span></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Equal Weighted -->
<div data-xshow="tab==='equal'" class="glass-2 p-5">
<h4 class="font-bold text-white mb-2">2. Equal Weighted</h4>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Invest EQUAL amount in EACH stock. Same weight regardless of price/size.</p>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 mb-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2">Method 1: Assume ₹6,000 in each</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Prices: A=10, B=20, C=30 | After 1yr: 11, 24, 31</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">Shares: A=600, B=300, C=200<br/>Final Value: 6,600+7,200+6,200 = ₹20,000<br/>Return = (20,000−18,000)/18,000 = <span class="num">11.11%</span></div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-cyan-300 mb-2">Method 2: Quick Method</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">A return: 10% | B return: 20% | C return: 3.33%</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 mt-1">Avg = (10+20+3.33)/3 = <span class="num">11.11%</span> ✓</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">⭐ KEY CHARACTERISTIC: Needs MOST FREQUENT Rebalancing</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Weights change as soon as prices move. NIFTY 50 Equal Weight rebalanced QUARTERLY (theoretically daily).</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-1">MCQ Example: Total Return with Dividends</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">P₀: 10, 20, 30. P₁+Div: 12.75, 20, 32.<br/>Returns: 27.5%, 0%, 6.67% → Avg = <span class="num">11.4%</span></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Market Cap -->
<div data-xshow="tab==='mcap'" class="glass-2 p-5">
<h4 class="font-bold text-white mb-2">3. Market Cap Weighted</h4>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Weight = Stock's Market Cap / Total Market Cap. Higher MCap → Higher weight.</p>
<div class="formula-box mb-3"><span class="tex">Market Cap = Price × Outstanding Shares</span></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 ring-em mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">⭐ KEY CHARACTERISTIC: MOMENTUM EFFECT</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">MCap ↑ → Weight ↑. Bigger gets bigger. Example: Yes Bank in NIFTY 50 when big, removed when small.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2">Worked Example</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Stock</th><th>P₀</th><th>Shares</th><th>MCap₀ (L)</th><th>P₁</th><th>MCap₁ (L)</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>MNO</td><td>2,500</td><td>5,000</td><td>125</td><td>2,700</td><td>135</td></tr>
<tr><td>QRS</td><td>3,500</td><td>7,500</td><td>262.5</td><td>2,500</td><td>187.5</td></tr>
<tr><td>XYZ</td><td>1,500</td><td>10,000</td><td>150</td><td>1,600</td><td>160</td></tr>
<tr><td class="font-bold">Total</td><td></td><td></td><td class="font-bold">537.5</td><td></td><td class="font-bold">482.5</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="calc-result mt-3 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Price Return:</b> (482.5−537.5)/537.5 = <span class="num">−10.23%</span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">With dividends 100, 150, 100 → New total = ₹508.75 L → <b>Total Return = −5.35%</b></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Free Float Market Cap -->
<div data-xshow="tab==='float'" class="glass-2 p-5">
<h4 class="font-bold text-white mb-2">4. Free Float Market Cap Weighted <span class="badge b-em ml-1">NIFTY 50 uses this</span></h4>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Excludes promoter holding. Only shares available to public are weighted.</p>
<div class="formula-box mb-3"><span class="tex">Free Float MCap = Market Cap × Public Holding %</span></div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-cyan-300 mb-2">Why This Matters: Reliance vs HDFC Bank</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Stock</th><th>MCap (₹L Cr)</th><th>Promoter %</th><th>Public %</th><th>Free Float MCap</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Reliance</td><td>17</td><td>~51%</td><td>~49%</td><td>₹8.33 L Cr</td></tr>
<tr><td>HDFC Bank</td><td>11</td><td>&lt;2%</td><td>~98%+</td><td class="text-emerald-300"><b>₹10.78 L Cr</b></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-2">→ HDFC Bank gets MORE weight in NIFTY 50 than Reliance!</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-1">NIFTY 50 Top Weights</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">1. HDFC Bank: 10.56% | 2. ICICI Bank: 8.32% | 3. Reliance: 8.27%</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">HDFC & ICICI are professionally managed — low promoter holding → high free float → higher weight.</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-2">Worked Example</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs mb-2">
<thead><tr><th>Stock</th><th>Shares</th><th>Public %</th><th>P₀</th><th>P₁</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>A</td><td>5,000</td><td>90%</td><td>40</td><td>45</td></tr><tr><td>B</td><td>2,000</td><td>100%</td><td>68</td><td>60</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">
<b>FF MCap₀:</b> A = 5,000×40×0.9 = ₹1,80,000 | B = 2,000×68×1.0 = ₹1,36,000 → Total = <span class="num">₹3,16,000</span><br/>
<b>FF MCap₁:</b> A = 5,000×45×0.9 = ₹2,02,500 | B = 2,000×60×1.0 = ₹1,20,000 → Total = <span class="num">₹3,22,000</span>
</div>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Return:</b> 6,000/3,16,000 ≈ <span class="num">2.06%</span> → Ending value of ₹100 portfolio = <span class="num">₹102.06</span></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Fundamental -->
<div data-xshow="tab==='fund'" class="glass-2 p-5">
<h4 class="font-bold text-white mb-2">5. Fundamental Weighted</h4>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Weight based on FUNDAMENTAL factors (most commonly: <span class="keyword">Earnings Yield</span> or Low PE).</p>
<div class="formula-box mb-3"><span class="tex">Earnings Yield = <span class="frac"><span>Earnings</span><span>Price</span></span> = <span class="frac"><span>1</span><span>PE</span></span></span></div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-cyan-300 mb-2">Rental Property Analogy</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th></th><th>Value</th><th>Rent</th><th>Yield</th><th>PE</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>Property A</td><td>₹100</td><td>₹10</td><td>10%</td><td>10x</td></tr><tr><td>Property B</td><td>₹100</td><td>₹20</td><td>20%</td><td>5x</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-2">→ Buy B (higher yield, lower PE, cheaper)</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-2">⭐ KEY CHARACTERISTICS</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li class="check-li"><span><b>Value Tilt:</b> More weight to cheaper stocks</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span><b>CONTRARIAN EFFECT:</b> If price rises too much → Earnings Yield falls → Weight DECREASES</span></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-2">Opposite of Market Cap (which has Momentum Effect)!</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Summary Table -->
<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Summary Table — All Weight Systems</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Weight System</th><th>Key Characteristics</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Price Weighted</b></td><td>Buy 1 share each; higher price = more weight. ⭐ <b>Divisor adjusts for stock split</b></td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Equal Weighted</b></td><td>Equal amount each; ⭐ Needs <b>MOST FREQUENT rebalancing</b></td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Market Cap Weighted</b></td><td>Weight ∝ MCap; ⭐ <b>MOMENTUM EFFECT</b> (bigger gets bigger)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Free Float MCap</b></td><td>Used by NIFTY 50; excludes promoter holding; higher public holding = higher weight</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Fundamental</b></td><td>Weight based on Earnings Yield; ⭐ <b>CONTRARIAN EFFECT</b> (Value Tilt)</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>


<!-- Weight Systems — Worked Numerical Examples -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Weight Systems — Worked Numerical Examples 🧮</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">1 · Price Weighted — return</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Buy 1 share of each. A: ₹100→₹110, B: ₹50→₹52.</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mt-1">
<li>• Begin = 100 + 50 = ₹150 · End = 110 + 52 = ₹162</li>
<li>• <b>Price Return</b> = (162−150)/150 = <span class="num">8%</span></li>
<li>• With ₹1 dividend each → End 164 → <b>Total Return</b> = 14/150 = <span class="num">9.33%</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2 · Equal Weighted — two methods</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">A: ₹10→₹11, B: ₹20→₹24, C: ₹30→₹31.</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mt-1">
<li>• <b>Method A</b> (₹6,000 each → ₹18,000): end 6,600+7,200+6,200 = 20,000 → (20,000−18,000)/18,000 = <span class="num">11.11%</span></li>
<li>• <b>Method B</b> (faster): average of returns 10%, 20%, 3.33% = <span class="num">11.11%</span></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Equal-weight return = simple average of constituent returns (no amount to assume).</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">3 · Market Cap Weighted — weights</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">A MCap ₹100 Cr, B MCap ₹50 Cr (total ₹150 Cr).</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mt-1">
<li>• Weight A = 100/150 = <span class="num">66.67%</span> · Weight B = 50/150 = <span class="num">33.33%</span></li>
<li>• MCap = Price × Shares Outstanding → bigger cap = bigger weight (<b>momentum</b>)</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-300 mb-2">4 · Price Weighted — stock-split divisor</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">P₀ = 10, 20, 60 → divisor 3 → index = 90/3 = <b>30</b>.</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mt-1">
<li>• C splits 3:1 → prices 10, 20, 20 (sum 50). Value must NOT jump, so set new divisor: 50/x = 30 → x = <span class="num">1.667</span></li>
<li>• Next day P₁ = 12, 19, 22 (sum 53) → index = 53/1.667 = <span class="num">31.79</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-300 mb-2">5 · Fundamental Weighted — earnings yield / P/E</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Weight by a fundamental such as <b>earnings yield = Earnings ÷ Price</b> (the inverse of P/E). Two ₹100 assets:</div>
<div class="overflow-x-auto">
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Asset</th><th>Price</th><th>Income</th><th>Earnings Yield</th><th>P/E</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>A</td><td>₹100</td><td>₹10</td><td>10%</td><td>10×</td></tr>
<tr><td>B</td><td>₹100</td><td>₹20</td><td>20%</td><td>5×</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-2"><b class="text-emerald-300">Value tilt:</b> more weight to the "cheaper" stock (higher earnings yield / lower P/E — here B). <b class="text-rose-300">Contrarian effect:</b> if a stock's price runs up too far, its weight FALLS — the opposite of market-cap's momentum.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Indexes 101 — what they measure & return types -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Indexes 101 — What They Measure &amp; Return Types</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">What an index represents</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Asset-class</b> performance (equity, real estate, commodities)</li>
<li>• The <b>whole security market</b> (Nifty 50, Sensex 30, S&amp;P 500)</li>
<li>• A <b>market segment</b> (Nifty Bank, Nifty IT, Nifty Auto)</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Built as a portfolio of stocks = <b>constituents</b>; changing them = <b>reconstitution</b> (like swapping players on a cricket team).</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Price vs Total return</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Price Return</b> = (P₁ − P₀) / P₀ — price move only</li>
<li>• <b>Total Return</b> = (P₁ + Dividends − P₀) / P₀ — includes dividends</li>
<li>• ₹100 → ₹110 = <b>10%</b> price; + ₹5 dividend = <b>15%</b> total</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Nifty 50 since inception ≈ 10% price return, ≈ 12.38% total return.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Index Construction Decisions & Reconstitution -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Index Construction — 4 Decisions</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 mb-5">

<!-- Rebalancing vs Reconstitution -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Rebalancing vs Reconstitution</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Reconstitution (Recomposition)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Replacing constituents based on eligibility. Market cap falls below threshold → <b class="text-rose-300">removed</b>; rises above → <b class="text-emerald-300">added</b>.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Rebalancing</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Adjusting weights back to target. Prices move → actual weights drift → sell overweight, buy underweight to restore targets (esp. equal-weighted indexes).</p>
</div>
</div>
<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Rebalancing during Reconstitution — funding the gap</h4>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• OUT: Wipro (FF MCap ₹50,000 Cr) → selling raises ₹50,000 Cr</li>
<li>• IN: Adani Power (FF MCap ₹90,000 Cr) → needs ₹90,000 Cr</li>
<li>• Gap of ₹40,000 Cr → raised by trimming the other 49 stocks</li>
</ul>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b class="text-emerald-300">Key:</b> when the incoming company has a higher weight than the outgoing one, existing constituents must also be SOLD to fund the difference.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- 5 Uses of Indexes -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">5 Uses of Security Market Indexes</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">1</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Reflect Market Sentiment</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Captures overall mood — war → Nifty falls; trade deal → Nifty rises.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">2</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Benchmark Active Managers</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Fund vs index: 9% vs 12% = underperform; 15% vs 12% = alpha.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">3</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Launch ETFs / Passive Funds</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">You CAN invest in Nifty 50 — via a Nifty 50 ETF that tracks it 1:1.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">4</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">PROXY for Asset Class</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">In asset-allocation models. Nifty 50 represents (not equals) Indian equity.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">5</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">PROXY for Systematic Risk</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">β = Cov(stock, market) ÷ Var(market); index is the "market" proxy.</div></div></div>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b class="text-amber-300">⚠ Exam trap:</b> uses 4 &amp; 5 MUST include the word <b>"PROXY"</b> — without it the answer is marked wrong.</div>
</div>

<!-- Equity Index Types — Style & Multi-Market -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Equity Index Types — Style &amp; Multi-Market</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Style Indexes</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Split by market cap, then by style (Value vs Growth). E.g. <b>Nifty 50 Value 20</b> = the 20 cheapest of the top 50.</p>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Value:</b> cheap valuations · <b>Growth:</b> expensive, future growth priced in</li>
<li>• Returns since inception: Nifty 50 <b>12.38%</b> vs Value 20 <b>17.59%</b></li>
<li>• Buffett-style value investing, but via an ETF (less risky than single stocks)</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Multi-Market Indexes</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Span multiple countries. E.g. <b>MSCI World Index</b> (Morgan Stanley) — 23 developed economies.</p>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Top holdings: NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft</li>
<li>• US ~72%, Japan 5%, UK 3%, Canada 3%, France 2%</li>
<li>• India is NOT included (developed markets only)</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b class="text-cyan-300">4 equity types:</b> Broad Market · Sectoral · Style · Multi-Market.</div>
</div>

<!-- Fixed Income Indexes -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Fixed Income (Bond) Indexes</h3>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-400 mb-3">Bond = you lend to a company/government, repaid with interest. Government is the biggest borrower.</p>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Classified 5 ways</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Issuer</b> — government vs non-government (corporate)</li>
<li>• <b>Collateral</b> — secured vs unsecured</li>
<li>• <b>Coupon</b> — high / low / zero coupon</li>
<li>• <b>Maturity</b> — 1yr, 2yr, 5yr, 10yr…</li>
<li>• <b>Credit risk</b> — govt ≈ zero; AAA/AA low; B/C/D high (higher risk → higher return)</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2"><b class="text-cyan-300">Aggregate index</b> = captures the TOTAL bonds issued in an economy.</div>
</div>
<div class="overflow-x-auto">
<table class="w-full text-xs">
<thead><tr class="text-left text-slate-400"><th class="p-2">Feature</th><th class="p-2">Equity (Nifty 50)</th><th class="p-2">Fixed Income</th></tr></thead>
<tbody class="text-slate-300">
<tr class="border-t border-white/10"><td class="p-2">Constituents</td><td class="p-2">50</td><td class="p-2">Thousands</td></tr>
<tr class="border-t border-white/10"><td class="p-2">Turnover</td><td class="p-2">Low</td><td class="p-2">Very high (bonds mature &amp; are replaced)</td></tr>
<tr class="border-t border-white/10"><td class="p-2">Liquidity</td><td class="p-2">Liquid</td><td class="p-2">Illiquid</td></tr>
<tr class="border-t border-white/10"><td class="p-2">Pricing</td><td class="p-2">Transparent, market</td><td class="p-2">Dealer-dependent</td></tr>
<tr class="border-t border-white/10"><td class="p-2">Replication</td><td class="p-2">Easy</td><td class="p-2">Very difficult</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b class="text-emerald-300">Why high turnover?</b> bonds have a finite life — they mature and EXIT, new issues ENTER. <b class="text-emerald-300">Why illiquid?</b> like property, you must ask a dealer for the price.</div>
</div>

<!-- Alternative Investment Indexes -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Alternative Investment Indexes</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-300 mb-2">Commodity</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Weighting problem</b> — no market-cap concept (gold vs crude vs silver?)</li>
<li>• Prices are <b>FUTURES</b>, not spot — cash-settled, no physical delivery</li>
<li>• MCX gold ≠ jeweller (spot) price — there's a difference</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-300 mb-2">Real Estate</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Appraisal Index</li>
<li>• Repeat-Sales Index</li>
<li>• Index of REITs</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">(Detail comes in Alternative Investments.)</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-300 mb-2">Hedge Fund</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Voluntary, self-reported returns</li>
<li>• <b>Upward / survivorship bias</b> — only good results reported</li>
<li>• No verification mechanism</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Exam traps -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">⚠ Exam Traps &amp; Critical Words</h3>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-2">
<li>• <b class="text-amber-300">"PROXY"</b> — required for the asset-class &amp; systematic-risk uses. Missing it = wrong.</li>
<li>• <b class="text-amber-300">"Free-Float Market Cap"</b> — Nifty 50 weights use free-float, not total market cap.</li>
<li>• Don't confuse <b>rebalancing</b> (restore weights) with <b>reconstitution</b> (change constituents).</li>
<li>• Commodity index prices are <b>futures</b>, not spot.</li>
<li>• Fixed-income indexes are hard to replicate; hedge-fund indexes are upward-biased.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch8" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">08</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 8 · Market Structure</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Market Organization & Structure</h2>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Functions of Financial System -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Functions of the Financial System</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">1. Facilitate Saving & Borrowing</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Savers deposit, banks lend to businesses (Tata, Reliance, Adani).</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Interest rates must be BALANCED:</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">
<li>• Too HIGH → Savers happy, businesses don't borrow</li>
<li>• Too LOW → Businesses borrow, savers don't deposit</li>
<li>• OPTIMAL → Both active</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2. Efficient Capital Allocation</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Money should NOT remain idle. Capital must flow to MOST PRODUCTIVE uses for economic growth.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">3. Key Entities</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<li>• SAVE — households</li>
<li>• BORROW — businesses, govt</li>
<li>• ISSUE EQUITY — companies</li>
<li>• MANAGE RISK — insurance</li>
<li>• EXCHANGE assets — exchanges</li>
<li>• FACILITATE — banks</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Asset Classifications -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-4">Classification of Assets and Markets (8 Pairs)</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">1. Financial vs Real Asset</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Financial:</b> Bank FD, Shares, Bonds, MFs</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Real:</b> Property, Gold, Commodities, Real Estate</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">2. Debt vs Equity</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Debt:</b> Fixed interest (6–7%), principal back. Bank FD</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Equity:</b> Dividend + Capital Appreciation (Buy ₹100, Sell ₹120 = ₹20 + Dividend)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Real Estate Analogy: Equity = Real Estate (rent+appr); Debt = FD (interest only)</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">3. Public vs Private Securities</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Public:</b> Listed (Reliance, TCS) — easily tradable</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Private:</b> Not listed — limited buyers</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">4. Physical vs Financial Derivatives</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Physical:</b> On commodities (Gold, Metal derivatives)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Financial:</b> On stocks (Reliance futures, Index futures)</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">5. Spot vs Future</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Spot:</b> Buy/sell NOW, immediate payment & delivery</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Future:</b> Buy/sell LATER (gold after 6 months)</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">6. Primary vs Secondary Market</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Primary:</b> Buy from COMPANY (IPO, Rights, Private Placement)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Secondary:</b> Buy from MARKET (NSE/BSE) — from other investors</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">7. Money vs Capital Market</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Money:</b> Short-term (&lt; 1 yr) — T-Bills, Commercial Paper</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Capital:</b> Long-term (≥ 1 yr) — Bonds, Stocks</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">8. Traditional vs Alternative</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Traditional:</b> Bank FD, Bonds, Stocks/Equity</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>Alternative:</b> Real Estate, Gold, Commodities, Bitcoin, Art, Wine</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Market Participants -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-4">Market Participants & Intermediaries</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2"><span class="lucide">👥</span><h4 class="font-bold text-white">1. Broker — Zerodha, 99acres</h4></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Provides <span class="keyword">PLATFORM only</span>. Connects buyer & seller at SAME TIME. Does NOT buy/sell itself. Earns commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2"><span class="lucide">🏪</span><h4 class="font-bold text-white">2. Dealer — Spinny, Car Dealers</h4></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Provides <span class="keyword">LIQUIDITY</span>. Connects at DIFFERENT times. BUYS from seller first, SELLS to buyer later. Takes INVENTORY RISK.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2">Vikas sells car to Spinny @ ₹50K → Spinny sells to Akash @ ₹60K (10 days) → ₹10K profit</div>
</div>
</div>

<table class="pretty mt-3 mb-4">
<thead><tr><th>Aspect</th><th class="text-emerald-300">BROKER</th><th class="text-cyan-300">DEALER</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Timing</td><td>Same time</td><td>Different time</td></tr>
<tr><td>Role</td><td>Platform only</td><td>Takes inventory</td></tr>
<tr><td>Price Risk</td><td>None</td><td>Bears price risk</td></tr>
<tr><td>Income</td><td>Commission/Fee</td><td>Spread/Profit</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2"><span class="lucide">↔️</span><h4 class="font-bold text-white">3. Arbitrageur</h4></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Exploits MISPRICING across markets. Buys CHEAP in one, sells EXPENSIVE in another. RISK-FREE profit. Makes markets EFFICIENT.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1"><b>Example:</b> Onions ₹10 (A), ₹15 (B) → buy A, sell B → ₹5 profit/kg</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2"><span class="lucide">🛡️</span><h4 class="font-bold text-white">4. Insurance Company</h4></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Creates <span class="keyword">DIVERSIFIED POOL OF RISK</span>. Multiple risk types, geographically diverse.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Only Kolkata insured → flood = huge loss. All India → risk spread.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2"><span class="lucide">🏛️</span><h4 class="font-bold text-white">5. Clearing House — NSCCL</h4></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Reduces <span class="keyword">COUNTERPARTY RISK</span>. Ensures buyer gets shares, seller gets payment. Promotes market integrity.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2"><span class="lucide">🌙</span><h4 class="font-bold text-white">6. ATS / Dark Pools — Bloomberg</h4></div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Platform for <span class="keyword">INSTITUTIONAL clients</span>. Less regulated, no public disclosure. Rakesh Jhunjhunwala deals directly with mutual funds via Bloomberg → no market impact.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Long vs Short -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Long Position, Short Position & Leverage</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">LONG (Bullish)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">BUY first, SELL later. Want price UP. FIX your COST.</p>
