<div class="text-xs text-slate-400"><b>Example:</b> Mom buys gold @ ₹14,200/g, sells @ ₹15,000/g → Profit ₹800</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">SHORT (Bearish)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">SELL first, BUY later. Want price DOWN. FIX your SELLING PRICE.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">
<b>Steps:</b><br/>
1. BORROW shares<br/>
2. SELL in market @ ₹100<br/>
3. Wait for price to fall to ₹80<br/>
4. BUY back @ ₹80<br/>
5. RETURN shares<br/>
<span class="text-emerald-300 font-bold">Profit = ₹20</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Leverage -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Leverage — The Catalyst</h3>
<div class="formula-box mb-3">
<span class="tex">Leverage Ratio = <span class="frac"><span>Asset</span><span>Equity</span></span></span>
<span class="tex">ROE with Leverage = Asset Return % × Leverage Ratio</span>
</div>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-4">Using BORROWED money to invest. Acts as catalyst: gains AND losses MAGNIFIED.</p>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Case 1 — No Leverage (100% Equity)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Asset = ₹100 | Equity = ₹100 | Debt = ₹0<br/>Leverage Ratio = 100/100 = <span class="num">1.0</span></div>
<table class="pretty text-xs mt-2">
<thead><tr><th>Scenario</th><th>Asset</th><th>ROE</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>+20% gain</td><td>₹120</td><td class="text-emerald-300">+20%</td></tr>
<tr><td>−20% loss</td><td>₹80</td><td class="text-rose-300">−20%</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Range: −20% to +20%</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Case 2 — With Leverage (60% E, 40% D, 0% int)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Asset = ₹100 | Equity = ₹60 | Debt = ₹40<br/>Leverage Ratio = 100/60 = <span class="num">1.6667</span></div>
<table class="pretty text-xs mt-2">
<thead><tr><th>Scenario</th><th>Net</th><th>ROE</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>+20% gain</td><td>₹80</td><td class="text-emerald-300">+33.33%</td></tr>
<tr><td>−20% loss</td><td>₹40</td><td class="text-rose-300">−33.33%</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-1">✓ Verification: 20% × 1.6667 = 33.33%</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">Comparison & Interpretation</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th></th><th>No Leverage</th><th>With Leverage</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Gain Scenario</td><td>+20%</td><td>+33.33%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Loss Scenario</td><td>−20%</td><td>−33.33%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Leverage Ratio</td><td>1.0</td><td>1.6667</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-2">✓ Gains AND losses both increased by 66.67%</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">For every ₹1 equity → control ₹1.6667 assets, borrowed ₹0.6667. Volatility amplified by 1.6667x.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Margin Call -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Margin Call — When Broker Calls For More Money</h3>
<div class="formula-box mb-4">
<span class="tex">P<sup>*</sup> = <span class="frac"><span>P<sub>0</sub> × (1 - Initial Margin)</span><span>1 - Maintenance Margin</span></span></span>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Intuition</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Numerator [P₀ × (1−IM)] = <b>LOAN AMOUNT</b></li>
<li>• Denominator [(1−MM)] = Maximum loan % allowed</li>
<li>• When loan % crosses maintenance threshold → <span class="warning">MARGIN CALL</span></li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Worked Example</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-3 space-y-0.5"><li>P₀ = ₹100</li><li>Initial Margin = 40%</li><li>Maintenance Margin = 25%</li></ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<div><b class="text-white">Step 1:</b> Loan = 100 × (1−0.4) = ₹60. Equity = ₹40.</div>
<div><b class="text-white">Step 2:</b> P* = (100 × 0.6) / (1 − 0.25) = 60/0.75 = <span class="num">₹80</span></div>
</div>
<div class="calc-result mt-2 text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Margin Call Price:</b> <span class="num">₹80.00</span></div>

<table class="pretty text-xs mt-3">
<thead><tr><th>Price</th><th>Loan</th><th>Loan %</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>₹100</td><td>₹60</td><td>60.0%</td><td class="text-emerald-300">Normal</td></tr>
<tr><td>₹90</td><td>₹60</td><td>66.67%</td><td>Monitoring</td></tr>
<tr><td>₹85</td><td>₹60</td><td>70.59%</td><td class="text-amber-300">Warning</td></tr>
<tr><td>₹80</td><td>₹60</td><td>75.00%</td><td class="text-rose-300 font-bold">MARGIN CALL</td></tr>
<tr><td>₹60</td><td>₹60</td><td>100.00%</td><td class="text-rose-300">Critical</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Participants by Behaviour -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Participants by Behaviour — Hedger, Investor, Trader, Arbitrageur</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-2">Hedger</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Takes an OFFSETTING position to REDUCE risk &amp; minimise uncertainty.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">E.g. health/car insurance; a US exporter hedging BRL depreciation with currency futures.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Arbitrageur</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Exploits MISPRICING across markets for RISK-FREE profit. Makes markets efficient.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Investor</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">BUYS &amp; HOLDS long-term. Uses <b>Fundamental Analysis</b> (company, industry, financials).</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">E.g. Buffett (Coca-Cola), Jhunjhunwala (Titan). Invests to risk appetite.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Trader</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Buys/sells/holds SHORT-term. Uses <b>Technical Analysis</b> (charts, moving averages, volume, candles).</p>
</div>
</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs mt-3">
<thead><tr><th>Participant</th><th>Horizon</th><th>Analysis</th><th>Goal</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Investor</td><td>Long-term</td><td>Fundamental</td><td>Capital appreciation</td></tr>
<tr><td>Trader</td><td>Short-term</td><td>Technical</td><td>Quick price-move profits</td></tr>
<tr><td>Hedger</td><td>As needed</td><td>Risk-based</td><td>Risk minimisation</td></tr>
<tr><td>Arbitrageur</td><td>Immediate</td><td>Price comparison</td><td>Risk-free profit</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<!-- ETFs -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs)</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">A <b>passive</b> fund that <b>replicates an index</b> and trades on an exchange like a stock. Created by mutual-fund companies, backed by real shares, very low expense ratio.</p>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">How an SBI Nifty 50 ETF works</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Collects ₹10,000 Cr → splits into units @ ₹10, lists on the exchange</li>
<li>• Invests the full amount in Nifty 50 stocks at the SAME weights (HDFC 10% → 10% of fund)</li>
<li>• As Nifty moves, the ETF value moves 1:1</li>
</ul>
</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th></th><th class="text-emerald-300">ETF (Passive)</th><th class="text-cyan-300">Active Mutual Fund</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Aim</td><td>MATCH the index</td><td>BEAT the index</td></tr>
<tr><td>Manager</td><td>Tracks index</td><td>Picks stocks</td></tr>
<tr><td>Expense ratio</td><td>Very low</td><td>Higher</td></tr>
<tr><td>Holdings</td><td>Transparent</td><td>Discretionary</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<!-- Open vs Close-ended -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Open-Ended vs Close-Ended Funds</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Open-Ended</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Transact DIRECTLY with the fund at <b>NAV</b>. Fund continuously issues/redeems units → size varies.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">E.g. Parag Parikh Flexi Cap — invest/redeem anytime at NAV.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Close-Ended</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Fixed units; trade in the <b>SECONDARY MARKET</b> at market price (premium/discount to NAV), NOT with the fund.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b class="text-emerald-300">Analogy:</b> Open-ended = buy direct from DLF; Close-ended = buy the flat from an existing owner.</div>
</div>

<!-- Forward vs Future -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Forward vs Future Contracts</h3>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th class="text-amber-300">Forward</th><th class="text-emerald-300">Future</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Venue</td><td>OTC (private)</td><td>Exchange</td></tr>
<tr><td>Terms</td><td>Customised</td><td>Standardised</td></tr>
<tr><td>Counterparty risk</td><td>HIGH</td><td>ZERO (clearing house)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Liquidity / exit</td><td>Low / difficult</td><td>High / easy</td></tr>
<tr><td>Margin</td><td>Negotiable</td><td>Mandatory (initial margin)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Regulation</td><td>Minimal</td><td>High</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b class="text-rose-300">Forward's problem:</b> hard to exit + counterparty risk. <b class="text-emerald-300">Future's edge:</b> standardised, no counterparty risk, transparent.</div>
</div>

<!-- Worked Numericals -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Worked Numericals — Leverage, Returns &amp; Margin</h3>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Q1 · Leverage ratio from initial margin</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">IM = 55% → Equity ₹55 on a ₹100 asset, Debt ₹45.<br/>Leverage = Asset/Equity = 100/55 = <span class="num">1.818</span> (also = 1 ÷ IM).</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Q2 · Leveraged return</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Buy 200 sh @ ₹50 = ₹10,000; Leverage 2.5 → Equity = 10,000/2.5 = ₹4,000, Debt ₹6,000.<br/>Sell @ ₹60 = ₹12,000; repay ₹6,000 → ₹6,000 left.<br/>Return = (6,000−4,000)/4,000 = <span class="num">+50%</span> (= 20% × 2.5).</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Q3 · Return with commission, dividend &amp; interest</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-0.5">
<div>Buy 500 sh @ ₹32 = ₹16,000; IM 75% → Equity ₹12,000, Debt ₹4,000. Buy commission ₹10.</div>
<div>Sell @ ₹28 = ₹14,000 − ₹10 sell commission = ₹13,990.</div>
<div>Repay debt + 2% interest = 4,000 + 80 = ₹4,080 → ₹9,910 left.</div>
<div>+ Dividend 500 × ₹0.55 = ₹275 → ₹10,185.</div>
<div>Outflow = 12,000 + 10 = ₹12,010. Return = (10,185 − 12,010)/12,010 ≈ <span class="num text-rose-300">−15.4%</span>.</div>
</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Buy commission ADDS to cost; sell commission SUBTRACTS; interest SUBTRACTS; dividend ADDS.</div>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-2">Q4 · Short-sale margin</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Short 200 sh @ ₹47 → proceeds ₹9,400 (held by lender). Margin 40% = <span class="num">₹3,760</span> you deposit on top. Margin protects the lender if price RISES.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">Q5 · Margin call price</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">P₀ = ₹25, IM 50%, MM 30%.<br/>P* = 25 × (1−0.50)/(1−0.30) = 12.5/0.70 = <span class="num">₹17.86</span>. Below this → margin call.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>


<!-- Execution Orders -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Execution Instructions — Orders</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">1. Market Order</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Buy/sell IMMEDIATELY at BEST available price. No price specified.</p>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-400 space-y-0.5">
<li>• Executes INSTANTLY</li>
<li>• Speed &gt; Price</li>
<li>• Use for urgent news, immediate execution</li>
<li class="text-rose-300">• Risk: May get worse price than expected</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2. Limit Order</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Buy/sell at SPECIFIC price or better. Only executes if market reaches your price.</p>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-400 space-y-0.5">
<li>• You SPECIFY exact price</li>
<li>• May or may not execute</li>
<li>• Default validity: SINGLE DAY</li>
<li>• Buy Bajaj @ ₹950 (CMP ₹1,000)</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">4 Sub-Types of Limit Orders</h4>
<div class="quote text-xs mb-3">Market = Bid ₹1,000 / Ask ₹1,010 (Best Bid: highest buyer | Best Ask: lowest seller)</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">A. Take the Market</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Price EQUALS or CROSSES best opposite quote. <b>EXECUTES IMMEDIATELY.</b></p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Buyer ≥ Best Ask | Seller ≤ Best Bid</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Buy ≥ ₹1,010 → fills @ ₹1,010</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">B. Make a New Market</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Price BETWEEN best bid & ask. Become SOLE best. <b>PENDING.</b></p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Buy @ ₹1,005 → market becomes 1,005 – 1,010</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-1">C. Make the Market</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Price EQUALS best bid or ask. JOIN existing queue. <b>PENDING.</b></p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Buy @ ₹1,000 → join buyer A at best bid</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-1">D. Behind the Market</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Price WORSE than best. <b>Far from execution.</b></p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Buyer &lt; Best Bid | Seller &gt; Best Ask</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Buy @ ₹950 → only fills if price falls</div>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Summary Table — Buyer Side (Market: Bid ₹1,000 | Ask ₹1,010)</h4>
<table class="pretty mb-3">
<thead><tr><th>Order Type</th><th>Buyer Price</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>TAKE MARKET</td><td>≥ ₹1,010</td><td class="text-emerald-300">EXECUTES immediately</td></tr>
<tr><td>MAKE NEW MARKET</td><td>₹1,001–1,009</td><td>PENDING, SOLE best bid</td></tr>
<tr><td>MAKE MARKET</td><td>= ₹1,000</td><td>PENDING, JOIN existing</td></tr>
<tr><td>BEHIND MARKET</td><td>&lt; ₹1,000</td><td>PENDING, far from execution</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Summary Table — Seller Side</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Order Type</th><th>Seller Price</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>TAKE MARKET</td><td>≤ ₹1,000</td><td class="text-emerald-300">EXECUTES immediately</td></tr>
<tr><td>MAKE NEW MARKET</td><td>₹1,001–1,009</td><td>PENDING, SOLE best ask</td></tr>
<tr><td>MAKE MARKET</td><td>= ₹1,010</td><td>PENDING, JOIN existing</td></tr>
<tr><td>BEHIND MARKET</td><td>&gt; ₹1,010</td><td>PENDING, far from execution</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<!-- Order Matching Principle -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Order Matching Principle (NSE/BSE)</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Key Rules</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li class="check-li"><span><b>Best Buyer:</b> Offers HIGHEST price</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span><b>Best Seller:</b> Offers LOWEST price</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>When Buyer's price ≥ Seller's price → ORDER EXECUTES</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Priority of Execution</div>
<ol class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li><span class="step-num">1</span> <b class="text-white ml-2">PRICE</b> — Best price gets executed first</li>
<li><span class="step-num">2</span> <b class="text-white ml-2">DISPLAY</b> — Displayed orders preferred over hidden</li>
<li><span class="step-num">3</span> <b class="text-white ml-2">TIME</b> — Earlier order preferred</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 mt-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">Bid Book — DESCENDING</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Highest bid at top: 1000, 990, 980...</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">Ask Book — ASCENDING</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Lowest ask at top: 1010, 1020, 1030...</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Display vs Hidden Orders -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Display vs Hidden Orders</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Display Order</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Quantity & price VISIBLE to all</li>
<li>• Gets PRIORITY over hidden at same price</li>
<li>• Example: "Buy 1000 @ ₹1000" — everyone sees</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Hidden Order</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• Quantity NOT visible</li>
<li>• Used by large investors</li>
<li>• Lower priority at same price</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b>Why Hide?</b> Large orders MOVE the market. If everyone knows you want 1 lakh shares, sellers raise prices. Hidden orders protect large traders from market impact.</div>
</div>

<!-- Validity Instructions -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Validity Instructions (When Order Expires)</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">1. Day Order (Default)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Valid for ONE trading day. Cancelled at market close. Most common.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">2. Good Till Cancelled (GTC)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Remains UNTIL YOU CANCEL. Across multiple days. "Buy at ₹900" stays active for weeks/months.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-1">3. Good On Open / At Open</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Executes at MARKET OPEN only.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">4. Good On Close / At Close</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Executes at MARKET CLOSE only.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 md:col-span-2">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-1">5. Immediate or Cancel (IOC)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Execute immediately OR cancel immediately. Partial fills are cancelled. "Buy 500 @ ₹100 — fill or cancel".</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Stop Loss Order -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Stop Loss Order</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-4">Limits losses by automatically selling (or buying) when price reaches trigger level.</p>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">1. Stop Loss SELL Order (For LONG)</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mb-2">
<li>• You OWN the stock (LONG)</li>
<li>• Fear: Price might FALL</li>
</ul>
<div class="glass-2 p-3 text-xs">
<b class="text-rose-300">Example:</b><br/>
Bought Bajaj Finance @ ₹900<br/>
Trigger: ₹850 | Limit: ₹840<br/>
When price hits ₹850 → system sells 840–850<br/>
<span class="text-rose-300">Max loss/share: ₹60 (900−840)</span>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2. Stop Loss BUY Order (For SHORT)</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mb-2">
<li>• You SHORT SOLD the stock</li>
<li>• Fear: Price might RISE</li>
</ul>
<div class="glass-2 p-3 text-xs">
<b class="text-cyan-300">Example:</b><br/>
Short sold @ ₹900<br/>
Trigger: ₹950 | Limit: ₹960<br/>
When price hits ₹950 → buys 950–960<br/>
<span class="text-cyan-300">Max loss/share: ₹60 (960−900)</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Primary Market -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Primary Market (Detailed)</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Where companies sell securities DIRECTLY to investors.</p>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-3 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">1. IPO</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">First time selling to public. Becomes publicly listed.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">2. Right Issue</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">New shares to EXISTING shareholders. Usually at DISCOUNT.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Trade ₹100, Rights ₹95</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-1">3. Private Placement / QIP</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Sold to QUALIFIED/INSTITUTIONAL investors only. Not general public.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Bajaj raises ₹100 Cr from mutual funds</div>
</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Investment Banking Services</h4>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">1. Underwritten Offering (Firm Commitment)</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mb-2">
<li>• Bank GUARANTEES to buy all shares</li>
<li>• Bank bears ALL risk</li>
<li>• Company gets GUARANTEED money Day 1</li>
</ul>
<div class="glass-2 p-3 text-xs">
<b class="text-emerald-300">SpaceX Example:</b><br/>
Wants ₹100 Cr → Citibank buys @ ₹90 Cr<br/>
Sells to public @ ₹100 Cr → Profit ₹10 Cr<br/>
If unsold → Citibank bears loss<br/>
SpaceX gets ₹90 Cr regardless<br/>
<span class="text-emerald-300">Used for: STRONG demand, sure-shot issues</span>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">2. Best Efforts Offering</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1 mb-2">
<li>• Bank acts as BROKER/AGENT only</li>
<li>• Charges COMMISSION on shares sold</li>
<li>• Company bears risk</li>
<li>• No guarantee</li>
</ul>
<div class="glass-2 p-3 text-xs">
<b class="text-cyan-300">Vikas Classes Example:</b><br/>
Wants ₹100 Cr → Citibank "I'll try" + Kotak "I'll try"<br/>
Citi sells ₹30 Cr, Kotak ₹10 Cr → Total ₹40 Cr<br/>
Banks get commission on sold amount only<br/>
<span class="text-cyan-300">Used for: UNCERTAIN demand, risky issues</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<table class="pretty mt-4">
<thead><tr><th>Aspect</th><th class="text-emerald-300">Underwritten</th><th class="text-cyan-300">Best Efforts</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Risk</td><td>Bank bears</td><td>Company bears</td></tr>
<tr><td>Guarantee</td><td>Yes (to company)</td><td>No</td></tr>
<tr><td>Bank's Role</td><td>Buys first</td><td>Agent only</td></tr>
<tr><td>Bank's Income</td><td>Spread (buy-sell)</td><td>Commission</td></tr>
<tr><td>Used For</td><td>Strong demand</td><td>Uncertain demand</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<!-- Market Types -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Types of Markets (5 Categories)</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">1. Order-Driven</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Order matching principle. No dealer in price setting.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">NSE, BSE</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">2. Quote-Driven (Dealer)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Dealers provide liquidity via inventory. Earn spread.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Spinny, OTC markets</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-1">3. Brokered</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Broker provides platform. Matches buyers/sellers. Commission.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Zerodha, 99acres</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">4. Call Market</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Trades at SPECIFIC TIMES, SINGLE UNIFORM PRICE.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Pre-open session (9:00–9:15 AM)</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-1">5. Continuous</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Trades CONTINUOUSLY. Real-time demand/supply.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Regular session 9:15 AM – 3:30 PM</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Opening Price Determination -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">How Opening Price Is Determined (Call Market Mechanism)</h3>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Market Timings</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>9:00–9:15 AM:</b> PRE-OPEN SESSION (Call Market) — orders collected, no trading</li>
<li>• <b>9:15:01 AM:</b> CALL MARKET — opening auction (1 sec)</li>
<li>• <b>9:15:02 AM – 3:30 PM:</b> CONTINUOUS MARKET</li>
<li>• <b>3:30 PM – 4:00 PM:</b> CLOSING SESSION</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-300 mt-3"><b>Method:</b> Cumulative demand & supply at each price level. Price with MAXIMUM tradable quantity is selected. All matched trades execute at SINGLE UNIFORM PRICE.</div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Detailed Worked Example</h4>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Buyers (Bid Book — Descending)</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Buyer</th><th>Qty</th><th>Price</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>A</td><td>7</td><td>₹12</td></tr>
<tr><td>B</td><td>15</td><td>₹11</td></tr>
<tr><td>C</td><td>2</td><td>₹10</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">Sellers (Ask Book — Ascending)</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Seller</th><th>Qty</th><th>Price</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Z</td><td>9</td><td>₹10</td></tr>
<tr><td>Y</td><td>6</td><td>₹11</td></tr>
<tr><td>X</td><td>2</td><td>₹12</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Step 1–3: Cumulative + Tradable</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Price</th><th>Cum. Buy</th><th>Cum. Sell</th><th>Tradable = MIN</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>₹12</td><td>7</td><td>17</td><td>MIN(7,17) = 7</td></tr>
<tr><td>₹11</td><td>22</td><td>15</td><td class="text-emerald-300 font-bold">MIN(22,15) = 15 ⭐ MAX</td></tr>
<tr><td>₹10</td><td>24</td><td>9</td><td>MIN(24,9) = 9</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="calc-result mb-3">
<div class="text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">⭐ Opening Price =</b> <span class="num">₹11</span></div>
<div class="text-sm"><b class="text-emerald-300">⭐ Max Tradable Qty =</b> <span class="num">15 shares</span></div>
</div>

<div class="glass-2 p-4">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Step 5: Allocation at ₹11</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<div>• Z sells all 9 shares @ ₹11</div>
<div>• Y sells 6 shares @ ₹11 → Total sold: 15</div>
<div>• A buys 7 @ ₹11 (wanted at ₹12 — BENEFIT)</div>
<div>• B buys 8 @ ₹11 (FAIR) → Total bought: 15</div>
</div>
<div class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-2"><b>Remaining after open:</b> B has 7 pending @ ₹11 | X has 2 @ ₹12 | C has 2 @ ₹10</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Continuous market begins at 9:15:02 AM with these pending orders.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Well-functioning Financial System -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Well-Functioning Financial System (4 Pillars)</h3>
<div class="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 text-center">
<div class="icon-tile mx-auto mb-2"><span class="lucide">🗂️</span></div>
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-white mb-1">Complete Markets</div>
<div class="text-[11px] text-slate-400">Borrowers borrow, savers save, balanced rates</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 text-center">
<div class="icon-tile mx-auto mb-2"><span class="lucide">🛣️</span></div>
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-white mb-1">Allocational Efficiency</div>
<div class="text-[11px] text-slate-400">Capital flows to most productive uses</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 text-center">
<div class="icon-tile mx-auto mb-2"><span class="lucide">•</span></div>
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-white mb-1">Informational Efficiency</div>
<div class="text-[11px] text-slate-400">Prices reflect all info quickly</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 text-center">
<div class="icon-tile mx-auto mb-2"><span class="lucide">⚙️</span></div>
<div class="text-sm font-bold text-white mb-1">Operational Efficiency</div>
<div class="text-[11px] text-slate-400">Low transaction costs, easy trading</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Role of Regulators -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Role of Regulators (SEBI)</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">✓ Objectives of Market Regulation</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-2">
<li class="check-li"><span><b class="text-white">Minimize Agency Problems</b><br/>Reduce conflicts (custodian issues, counterparty risk)</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span><b class="text-white">Ensure Fair & Orderly Markets</b><br/>No manipulation, transparent operations, equal opportunity</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span><b class="text-white">Protect Unsophisticated Investors</b><br/>Retail protection, ban misleading influencers, accurate info</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-400 mb-2">✗ NOT an Objective</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-2">
<li class="x-li"><span><b>Guarantee returns to investors</b></span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span><b>Ensure risk-free rate of return</b></span></li>
<li class="x-li"><span><b>Make markets profitable</b></span></li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-3">Regulator's job is to make market <span class="hl">EFFICIENT</span>, not profitable.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch9" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">09</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 9 · Company Analysis</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Company Analysis — Past &amp; Present</h2>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Overview</h3>
<ul class="text-sm text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li class="check-li"><span><b class="text-white">5 Learning Outcome Statements</b> covered</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Mainly a <span class="keyword">theory-based</span> chapter — no heavy calculations</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Focus: how equity analysts analyze companies, forecast revenues, evaluate costs &amp; assess business models</span></li>
</ul>
</div>

<!-- Concept A -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Concept A · Equity Research Reports</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">An <span class="keyword">Equity Research Report</span> is a detailed analysis where the analyst understands the products, identifies competitive advantages, analyzes ratios, builds <b class="text-white">projected financials</b>, performs <b class="text-white">valuation</b> to reach a <span class="keyword">Target Price</span>, and gives a <b class="text-white">Buy/Sell/Hold</b> call.</p>
<div class="quote text-xs">💡 <b>Example:</b> Reliance trades ₹1,300, target ₹1,400 → <b class="text-emerald-300">Buy</b> (upside). Target ₹1,000 → <b class="text-rose-300">Don't buy</b> (downside risk).</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Two Types of Reports</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Initiating Coverage</th><th>Subsequent Report</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>First-time, detailed &amp; comprehensive report</td><td>Update to existing coverage</td></tr>
<tr><td>Full company description, industry overview, competitive positioning, ESG, detailed valuation</td><td>Triggered by new data; updates only recommendation, target price, rationale &amp; model</td></tr>
<tr><td>Audience: those <b>not</b> yet knowledgeable about the company</td><td>For existing followers</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3 ring-em"><div class="text-xs text-amber-300"><b>⚠ Subsequent reports do NOT include:</b> company description, competitive positioning, industry overview, ESG.</div></div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Components of an Initiating Coverage Report</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">1. Front Matter</b></td><td>Company name, analyst, CMP, target price, recommendation</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">2. Rationale</b></td><td>Reasons behind the Buy/Sell/Hold call</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">3. Company Description</b></td><td>Products, services, business model</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">4. Industry &amp; Competitive Positioning</b></td><td>Industry analysis + competitive advantages</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">5. Financial Analysis</b></td><td>Ratios, projected statements, valuation</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">6. ESG Factors</b></td><td>Environmental, Social, Governance</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">7. Risk Factors</b></td><td>Upside/downside risks that could change the rating</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">ESG Factors</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>E · Environmental</th><th>S · Social</th><th>G · Governance</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Impact of products on the environment (paper cuts trees, diesel, cigarettes/liquor)</td><td>Impact on society — beneficial or harmful?</td><td>Quality of management &amp; compliance (violating regulator norms = bad governance)</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-1">Risk Factors</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Identify both <b>upside &amp; downside</b> risks that could change your rating later (e.g., a new cloud technology disrupting Infosys).</p>
<p class="text-xs text-amber-300 mt-1">⭐ Risk factors appear in <b>BOTH</b> Initiating Coverage AND Subsequent reports.</p>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Concept B -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Concept B · Business Model</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">Understand what the company sells, who the <span class="keyword">customers</span> and major <span class="keyword">suppliers</span> are, and the <span class="keyword">payment terms</span>.</p>
<div class="quote text-xs mb-4">💡 <b>Example (a CFA coaching business):</b> Product = coaching · Customers = commerce students · Supplier = LMS provider · Payment terms = how fees are charged.</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3">Four Sources of Data</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Source</th><th>Description</th><th>Example</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">1. Company-Provided</b></td><td>Annual reports, investor presentations</td><td>Company's own annual report</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">2. Public Third-Party</b></td><td>Free data sources</td><td>News articles, free research</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">3. Proprietary Third-Party</b></td><td><b>Paid</b> research reports</td><td>CRISIL, ICRA, Bloomberg</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">4. Proprietary Primary</b></td><td><b>Self-conducted</b> research</td><td>Visiting cinemas, checking ticket sales</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Revenue Forecasting — Two Approaches</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Top-Down</th><th>Bottom-Up</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Starts with the <b>macroeconomic</b> environment</td><td>Starts <b>directly</b> with company data</td></tr>
<tr><td>Used for <b>large</b> companies</td><td>Used for <b>ALL</b> companies (especially small)</td></tr>
<tr><td>GDP growth → sector share → company share → revenue</td><td>Last year's revenue → # students → fee/student → forecast</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3 ring-em"><div class="text-xs text-amber-300">⭐ <b>Key rule:</b> Small companies → only <b>Bottom-Up</b> works. Large companies → <b>both</b>.</div></div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Pricing Power</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Has Pricing Power</th><th>No Pricing Power</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Low competition</td><td>High competition</td></tr>
<tr><td>High barriers to entry</td><td>Low barriers to entry</td></tr>
<tr><td>High switching costs</td><td>Easy to switch</td></tr>
<tr><td>No close substitutes</td><td>Many substitutes</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3"><b>Examples —</b> <b class="text-rose-300">No power:</b> CFA teachers, cab aggregators (price-sensitive). <b class="text-emerald-300">Has power:</b> electricity company (you can't refuse it), large FMCG with strong distribution (HUL).</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Market Share vs Market Size</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Term</th><th>Definition</th><th>Formula</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Market Size</b></td><td>Total revenue of ALL companies in that category</td><td>Σ competitors' revenue</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Market Share</b></td><td>One company's portion of the market</td><td>Company Revenue ÷ Market Size</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-1">Worked Example — Market Size</div>
<div class="formula-box text-xs mt-2">Market Size = Revenue ÷ Market Share = 500m ÷ 0.10 = ₹5,000m = ₹5 billion</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Note: 1 billion = 1,000 million.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Concept C -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Concept C · Cost Analysis</h3>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Fixed Cost</th><th>Variable Cost</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Does <b>NOT change</b> with output</td><td><b>Changes</b> with output</td></tr>
<tr><td>Office rent (fixed regardless of students)</td><td>Calculators (1 student = 1 calculator)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Paid even if <b>revenue is ZERO</b></td><td>Zero if output is zero</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Which Structure Is Better?</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Small Companies</th><th>Large Companies</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b>Variable costs preferred</b> — downside protected</td><td>Can handle fixed costs (stable revenue)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Max loss = break-even (₹0)</td><td>Can leverage fixed costs for higher profit</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3">🍽️ <b>Restaurant:</b> fixed rent ₹20 lakh → lose ₹20 lakh even at ₹0 revenue. Variable rent (10% of revenue) → if revenue = 0, rent = 0. <b class="text-emerald-300">Small/new businesses prefer variable costs</b>; fixed costs create leverage risk.</div>
</div>

<!-- Concept D -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Concept D · Leverage Analysis</h3>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mb-4 ring-em"><div class="text-sm text-amber-300 font-bold">"In finance, Fixed Cost is known as LEVERAGE."</div></div>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Operating Leverage</th><th>Financial Leverage</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Fixed costs of <b>operations</b> (rent, salaries)</td><td>Fixed costs of <b>financing</b> (loan interest)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Measured by <b>DOL</b> · amplifies EBIT</td><td>Measured by <b>DFL</b> · amplifies EAT</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Three Leverage Ratios</h4>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4"><div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-1">DOL</div><div class="formula-box text-xs">%Δ EBIT ÷ %Δ Sales<br>= Contribution ÷ EBIT</div><div class="text-[11px] text-slate-400 mt-1">Contribution = Revenue − Variable Cost</div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4"><div class="text-xs font-bold text-cyan-300 mb-1">DFL</div><div class="formula-box text-xs">%Δ EAT ÷ %Δ EBIT<br>= EBIT ÷ EBT</div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4"><div class="text-xs font-bold text-violet-300 mb-1">DTL</div><div class="formula-box text-xs">%Δ EAT ÷ %Δ Sales<br>= DOL × DFL</div></div>
</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Numerical Example</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Particulars</th><th>2015</th><th>2016</th><th>% Change</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Units Sold</td><td>100</td><td>120</td><td class="num">+20%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Revenue</td><td>₹1,000</td><td>₹1,200</td><td class="num">+20%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Variable Cost</td><td>₹200</td><td>₹240</td><td class="num">+20%</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Contribution</b></td><td><b>₹800</b></td><td><b>₹960</b></td><td class="num">+20%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Operating Fixed Cost</td><td>₹50</td><td>₹50</td><td>0%</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>EBIT</b></td><td><b>₹750</b></td><td><b>₹910</b></td><td class="num">+21.33%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Interest</td><td>₹70</td><td>₹70</td><td>0%</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>EBT</b></td><td><b>₹680</b></td><td><b>₹840</b></td><td class="num">+23.53%</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>EAT</b> (after 10% tax)</td><td><b>₹612</b></td><td><b>₹756</b></td><td class="num">+23.53%</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table class="pretty mt-3">
<thead><tr><th>Ratio</th><th>Calculation</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b>DOL</b></td><td>800 ÷ 750</td><td class="num">1.0667</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>DFL</b></td><td>750 ÷ 680</td><td class="num">1.1029</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>DTL</b></td><td>1.0667 × 1.1029</td><td class="num">1.1765</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-3">⚠️ <b>Double-edged sword:</b> Sales ↑20% → profit ↑23.53% (good); Sales ↓20% → profit ↓23.53% (bad). We dislike volatility, so small firms avoid fixed costs. If ALL costs were variable → DOL = DFL = DTL = 1 (no amplification).</div>

<h4 class="sub-title mb-3 mt-6">Economies of Scale vs Scope</h4>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Economies of Scale</th><th>Economies of Scope</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Manufacturing gets <b>more efficient</b>; per-unit cost <b>falls</b> as output rises</td><td>Add <b>new products</b> using existing infrastructure; costs don't rise proportionally</td></tr>
<tr><td>Making rotis — each takes less time</td><td>Teaching CFA + adding Financial Modeling in the same office</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="glass-2 p-3 mt-2"><div class="text-xs text-emerald-300">Both → profit margins <b>increase</b>.</div></div>
</div>

<!-- Concept E -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Concept E · Cash Conversion Cycle</h3>
<div class="formula-box text-sm mb-3">Cash Conversion Cycle = Debtor Days + Inventory Days − Creditor Days</div>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Debtor Days</b></td><td>Days customers take to pay you (money to receive)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Inventory Days</b></td><td>Days to sell inventory (money stuck in stock)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Creditor Days</b></td><td>Days you take to pay suppliers (money you hold)</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table class="pretty mt-3">
<thead><tr><th>Cycle</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-rose-300">Positive</b></td><td>Money is stuck in the business</td></tr>
<tr><td>Zero</td><td>Neutral</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-emerald-300">Negative</b></td><td>You hold others' money — <b>BEST</b> (bargaining power)</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold text-emerald-300 mb-1">Unilever (2016)</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Debtor 20 + Inventory 52 = 72 days stuck; Creditor 140 → <b class="num">CCC = −66 days</b>. Others owe Unilever money for 66 days → market leadership &amp; bargaining power.</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2"><b>Haldiram's:</b> Debtor 0 (cash only) + Inventory 0 (sells instantly) − Creditor 40 → <b class="num">CCC = −40 days</b> — excellent.</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Practice -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-4">Practice Questions</h3>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q1: Which statement about a subsequent report is MOST accurate?</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">✅ It updates the recommendation in light of new data.<br>❌ "Primary audience is those not knowledgeable" and "provides industry overview / competitive positioning / ESG" belong to <b>Initiating Coverage</b>.</div></details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q2: Research data from Bloomberg is what type?</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">✅ <b>Proprietary Third-Party Data</b> (paid, third-party).</div></details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q3: Revenue ₹500m, market share 10% — find market size.</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">Market Size = 500m ÷ 0.10 = <b class="num">₹5,000m = ₹5 billion</b>.</div></details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q4: Units 10,000; price ₹5; VC ₹3; op-fixed ₹8,000 — find DOL.</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">Revenue ₹50,000; VC ₹30,000; Contribution ₹20,000; EBIT ₹12,000.<br>DOL = Contribution ÷ EBIT = 20,000 ÷ 12,000 = <b class="num">1.667</b>.</div></details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q5: Upside/downside risks are included in…</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">✅ <b>Both</b> Initiating Coverage AND Subsequent reports.</div></details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q6: A natural-resource company with cheap energy sells output at…</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">✅ <b>Market Price</b> — but a lower input cost means <b>better margins</b> (e.g., Tata Motors buying steel from Tata Steel).</div></details>
<details class="glass-2 p-4 mb-2"><summary class="flex items-center justify-between"><span class="text-sm font-semibold text-white">Q7: First step in a company's capital investment?</span><span class="lucide">▸</span></summary><div class="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-300">✅ <b>Identify / evaluate where the company can invest</b>. Order: identify opportunities → forecast cash flows → compare profitability → invest where highest.</div></details>
</div>

<!-- Summary + Exam -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Quick Revision Summary</h3>
<table class="pretty">
<thead><tr><th>Concept</th><th>Key Points</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Research Reports</b></td><td>Initiating (detailed, first time) vs Subsequent (update only)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Business Model</b></td><td>Products, customers, suppliers, payment terms</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Data Sources</b></td><td>Company → Public → Proprietary third-party → Primary research</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Revenue Forecast</b></td><td>Top-down (macro → company) vs Bottom-up (company directly)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Pricing Power</b></td><td>Low competition + high barriers + no substitutes</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Costs</b></td><td>Fixed = leverage (risky for small cos); Variable = safer</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Leverage</b></td><td>DOL = Contribution/EBIT · DFL = EBIT/EBT · DTL = DOL × DFL</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Economies</b></td><td>Scale = lower per-unit cost; Scope = new products, same infrastructure</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Cash Conversion</b></td><td>Negative = best (holding others' money); Positive = money stuck</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 mt-4 ring-em">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-400 mb-1">🎯 Exam Strategy</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li class="check-li"><span>Theory-heavy chapter — focus on <b>concepts, not calculations</b>.</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Curriculum case studies are <b>not</b> tested in MCQs — skim them.</span></li>
<li class="check-li"><span>Do the Learning Ecosystem questions after this revision.</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch10" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">10</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 10 · Industry Analysis</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Industry &amp; Competitive Analysis</h2>
</div>
</div>

<!-- 5 Steps -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">The 5 Steps of Industry Analysis</h3>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-400 mb-4">Before valuing a company (Maruti, HUL…), first understand its industry and its competitive position.</p>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">1</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Define the industry</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Which industry does it operate in? (PW → Education, Maruti → Autos)</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">2</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Survey the industry</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Its size, growth, profitability &amp; trends over time.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">3</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Analyse industry structure</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Structure → profitability. Tool: <b class="text-emerald-300">Porter's Five Forces</b>.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">4</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Analyse external forces</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">"Industry themes." Tool: <b class="text-emerald-300">PESTLE</b>.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">5</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Competitive strategy</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Cost leadership · Differentiation · Focus.</div></div></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Company types + size + market share -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Industry Size, Company Types &amp; Market Share</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Growth vs Mature</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Growth:</b> grow FASTER than the economy (Zepto, PW, new entrants)</li>
<li>• <b>Mature:</b> grow ≈ economy (usually &lt;10%) — HUL, TCS, Reliance</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Cyclical vs Defensive</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Cyclical:</b> earnings VOLATILE, cycle/rate-sensitive — autos (Maruti), DLF, steel, industrials</li>
<li>• <b>Defensive:</b> earnings STABLE regardless of economy — FMCG, pharma, utilities</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Rates ↓ → more cars/homes bought → Maruti/DLF earnings ↑ (and vice-versa).</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mt-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Size &amp; Market Share</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Industry size</b> = total annual sales of the product across the whole industry (India passenger vehicles = ₹100 Cr).</li>
<li>• <b>Market share</b> = one company's % of that industry revenue (Maruti 10% of ₹100 Cr = ₹10 Cr).</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Concentration + HHI -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Industry Concentration &amp; the HHI</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">High concentration</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1"><li>• Few players rule (Telecom: Jio 55%, Airtel 45%)</li><li>• <b>Pricing power: YES</b> → strong, stable profits</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-300 mb-2">Low concentration</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1"><li>• Many players, nobody has power (thousands of tutors)</li><li>• <b>Pricing power: NO</b> → weak, unstable profits</li></ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">HHI — Herfindahl-Hirschman Index</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-1">Square each player's % share (as a whole number) and add them up.</p>
<table class="pretty text-xs mt-1">
<thead><tr><th>HHI</th><th>Concentration</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>&lt; 1,500</td><td>Low (many players, no power)</td></tr>
<tr><td>1,500 – 2,500</td><td>Moderate</td></tr>
<tr><td>&gt; 2,500</td><td>Highly concentrated (few players rule)</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-2"><b class="text-emerald-300">Examples:</b> Telecom 55²+45² = <span class="num">5,050</span>. Shares 50/30/20 → 2,500+900+400 = <span class="num">3,800</span>. <b>More concentrated → better profits.</b></div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Classification / comparables -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Finding Comparables &amp; Classification (GICS)</h3>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">GICS hierarchy — remember the order</div>
<div class="text-sm text-white font-bold text-center py-1">Sector → Industry Group → Industry → Sub-Industry</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Classified by <b>products &amp; services</b>. Screening software (Capital IQ) filters on GICS to find comparables — JK Tyre → Auto Ancillary → Tyre → heavy-duty (MRF, Ceat, Apollo).</div>
</div>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Other systems &amp; limits</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1"><li>• ICB (used by indexes), RBICS</li><li>• <b>Commercial</b> (GICS) updated MORE often than <b>government</b> systems</li><li>• Multi-product firms get misclassified (Reliance = oil OR telecom?)</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-300 mb-2">⚠ Grouping by geography</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1"><li>• By <b>head-office</b> location or <b>listing</b> location ✓</li><li>• <b>NEVER by revenue geography</b> (least likely) ✗</li></ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Tata Motors earns via JLR (UK/China) yet lists as India; TCS earns from US/EU.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Porter's Five Forces -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Porter's Five Forces (structure → profitability)</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 mb-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">1</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Threat of new entrants</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">How easy to enter? (licences, capital)</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">2</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Threat of substitutes</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Can another product replace yours?</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">3</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Bargaining power of buyers</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Fewer, bigger buyers = more power.</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">4</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Bargaining power of suppliers</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Can suppliers pressure you?</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">5</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Rivalry among competitors</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">How tough is existing competition?</div></div></div>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Jio:</b> hard to enter; buyers &amp; suppliers powerless (crores of each); only substitutes (Starlink) &amp; rivalry (Airtel) hurt → <b>3 of 5 in favour → high profitability.</b> <b class="text-rose-300">A tutor:</b> easy entry, many substitutes, few students, high rivalry → low profitability. Power depends on NUMBERS.</div>
</div>

<!-- PESTLE + innovation -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">PESTLE (external forces / "industry themes")</h3>
<div class="overflow-x-auto mb-3">
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Letter</th><th>Factor</th><th>Example</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b>P</b></td><td>Political</td><td>Election-time price controls; coaching norms</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>E</b></td><td>Economic</td><td>Interest rates → hits Maruti, DLF</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>S</b></td><td>Social</td><td>Liquor, cigarettes viewed negatively</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>T</b></td><td>Technological</td><td>AI threatening IT (TCS, Infosys)</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>L</b></td><td>Legal</td><td>Patents/copyright — pharma, films, music piracy</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>E</b></td><td>Environmental</td><td>Paper firms cut trees → heavy env. impact</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mb-3">Also a <b>Demographic</b> external factor — a country's age/gender mix affects industry growth.</div>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-300 mb-2">Sustaining innovation</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">You IMPROVE your own product; you don't harm others (a tutor upgrading webcam → proper camera). Defensive.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-300 mb-2">Disruptive innovation ("Innovator's Dilemma")</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Your move DISRUPTS existing businesses (PW cheap coaching; AI vs TCS/Infosys; a cheap legal-forms app vs law firms).</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Competitive strategies -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Three Generic Competitive Strategies</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Cost Leadership</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Sell very cheap to a LARGE market (DMart, Jio). Needs low cost → economies of scale, efficiency, favourable raw-material access.</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">⚠ NOT customer service / proximity (DMart stores are far, yet cheap).</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Differentiation</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Claim your product is different/better (every toothpaste "has salt"; a tutor teaches "differently").</p>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">⚠ Risk: becomes too EXPENSIVE while trying to be different.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Focus (Niche)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Target a small/niche segment only (Gucci, Rolls-Royce). Premium positioning, very limited customer base.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Exam map -->
<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">⚠ Exam Memory Map</h3>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-2">
<li>• <b class="text-cyan-300">Concentration</b> → measured by the <b>HHI</b>.</li>
<li>• <b class="text-cyan-300">Profitability / structure</b> → <b>Porter's Five Forces</b>.</li>
<li>• <b class="text-cyan-300">External themes</b> → <b>PESTLE</b>.</li>
<li>• Grouping by geography → <b>never</b> by revenue geography.</li>
<li>• Cost leadership → high volume + efficiency, <b>not</b> customer service/proximity.</li>
<li>• NOT a Porter force: barriers to EXIT, power of regulators, company life-cycle position.</li>
<li>• GICS classifies by <b>products/services</b>, updated more often than government systems.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>

<section id="ch11" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-emerald-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 flex items-center justify-center font-black text-emerald-300">11</div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-emerald-400 font-bold">Chapter 11 · Forecasting · 11–14%</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Company Analysis — Forecasting</h2>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Why We Forecast — the Market Prices the Future</h3>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-300 mb-3">To value a share you forecast its future financial statements — because a share moves on <b>expected future profits &amp; cash flow</b>, not today's. The market reacts <b>spontaneously and in advance</b>.</p>
<div class="quote text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Example:</b> TCS &amp; Infosys fell &gt;50% from highs — not because profits dropped yet, but because AI put a question mark on future profits. Price fell <b>before</b> the profit decline. Everything depends on <b>profitability &amp; cash flow</b>.</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">What to Forecast — Revenue Drives Everything</h3>
<div class="glass-2 p-5 mb-3">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">The one rule</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300"><b>REVENUE is the only item you forecast independently.</b> Everything else is expressed <b>relative to revenue</b>: expenses = % of sales · working capital = % of sales · capex = % of sales.</p>
</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Category</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Examples</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">With clear drivers</b></td><td>Predictable, measurable</td><td>Revenue, COGS, fixed SG&amp;A</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Without clear drivers</b></td><td>Irregular, non-recurring</td><td>Consulting/commission income, one-time gains</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Summary items</b></td><td>Calculated results</td><td>Gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT, EBT, EAT, FCF</td></tr>
<tr><td><b class="text-white">Ad-hoc items</b></td><td>Not in FS but material</td><td>Contingent liabilities, legal cases, mgmt changes</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Forecasting Revenue — Bottom-Up vs Top-Down</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Bottom-Up (company-specific)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">Units × price. E.g. 100 students × ₹100 = ₹10,000; next year 110 × ₹105 = ₹11,550. Best for small players / specific business units.</p>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-violet-400 mb-2">Top-Down (macro → micro)</div>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300">GDP growth → sector's share of GDP → company's market share. Best for large / macro-sensitive firms (Maruti, HUL). Big firms use BOTH.</p>
</div>
</div>
<table class="pretty text-xs">
<thead><tr><th>Revenue method</th><th>When to use</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Historical data</td><td>Stable companies, consistent patterns</td></tr>
<tr><td>Management guidance</td><td>When the company gives growth guidance (e.g. Accenture 2–4%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Analyst discretion</td><td>Cyclical / volatile firms where history is unreliable</td></tr>
<tr><td>Top-Down</td><td>Large, macro-sensitive businesses</td></tr>
<tr><td>Bottom-Up</td><td>Small companies, specific product lines</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Forecasting Costs — COGS &amp; SG&amp;A</h3>
<div class="formula-box mb-3"><span class="tex">COGS = Sales × (1 - Gross Profit Margin)</span></div>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">COGS — % of sales</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Defensive</b> (HUL/FMCG): margins stable (47–52%) → use historical average</li>
<li>• <b>Cyclical</b> (Tata Steel): P&amp;L volatile → analyst discretion + research</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">HUL profits climb steadily; Tata Steel swings from +₹4.8L to −₹40k → unpredictable.</div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">SG&amp;A — mostly fixed</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Fixed SG&amp;A</b> (salaries, rent) → grow with <b>inflation</b> (~5%)</li>
<li>• <b>Selling &amp; distribution</b> → model as % of sales (variable)</li>
<li>• <b>Agent commission</b> → % of revenue</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Revenue doubles → staff salary does NOT double; it grows with inflation only.</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">The 5 Forecasting Methods + Convergence</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 mb-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">1</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Historical data</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Project past trends — stable/defensive firms</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">2</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Base rate &amp; convergence</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Abnormal growth reverts to the historical average</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">3</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Management guidance</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Non-recurring items, capex plans</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">4</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Analyst discretion</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Cyclical / volatile companies</div></div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4 flex items-start gap-3"><span class="step-num">5</span><div><b class="text-white text-sm">Top-Down / Bottom-Up</b><div class="text-xs text-slate-400">Revenue forecasting (macro / micro)</div></div></div>
</div>
<div class="quote text-xs"><b class="text-emerald-300">Convergence (Muthoot):</b> gold rose ~50%, profit grew 100% (EPS ₹132→₹263) — but next year won't repeat. Growth reverts to the historical ~11–12% (the analyst 2027 forecast implies only 11%). <b>What happened historically eventually returns.</b></div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Balance-Sheet Forecasting</h3>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-400 mb-2">Fixed assets (capex)</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Maintenance capex</b> = depreciation grown by inflation (dep ₹100 → ₹105). Depreciation = consumption of plant.</li>
<li>• <b>Growth capex</b> = ask management (new factories? expansion?) → add to maintenance.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-2">Working capital</div>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-1">
<li>• <b>Debtors</b> → % of Sales</li>
<li>• <b>Creditors</b> → % of Purchases</li>
<li>• <b>Inventory</b> → % of COGS</li>
<li>• <b>Debt &amp; equity</b> → historical leverage + mgmt guidance</li>
</ul>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Sales ₹100→₹150 (+50%), debtors stay 10% of sales → ₹10→₹15 (+50%).</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">Sensitivity &amp; Scenario Analysis</h3>
<p class="text-xs text-slate-300 mb-2">Assumptions aren't precise, so you give a <b>range</b>, not a single number. Build three cases:</p>
<div class="grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-3 mb-3">
<div class="glass-2 p-4"><div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-cyan-400 mb-1">Base</div><div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Inflation 5%, CoE 15%</div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4"><div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-emerald-300 mb-1">Optimistic</div><div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Inflation 4%, CoE 14%</div></div>
<div class="glass-2 p-4"><div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-rose-300 mb-1">Pessimistic</div><div class="text-xs text-slate-300">Inflation 7%, CoE 17%</div></div>
</div>
<div class="glass-2 p-5">
<div class="text-xs font-bold uppercase text-amber-300 mb-2">Compare with the market-implied forecast</div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-300">HDFC Bank ₹829.30 · trailing P/E 16.84× → E₀ = 829.30/16.84 = ₹49.24 · forward P/E 15.20× → E₁ = 829.30/15.20 = ₹54.55 → <b>market-implied growth = (54.55−49.24)/49.24 = <span class="num">10.8%</span></b>.</div>
<div class="quote text-xs mt-2">If your forecast says 15% but the market implies 10.8% → either the market undervalues it, or your assumptions are too optimistic.</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="glass p-6 md:p-8 mb-5">
<h3 class="sub-title mb-3">⚠ Exam Key Points</h3>
<ul class="text-xs text-slate-300 space-y-2">
<li>• <b>Revenue</b> is the only independently-forecast item; everything else is % of sales.</li>
<li>• <b>Cyclical / volatile</b> firm → <b>analyst discretion</b> (not history, not mgmt guidance).</li>
<li>• <b>Capex</b> → <b>management guidance</b> (only they know expansion plans).</li>
<li>• <b>Summary item</b> example → <b>Free Cash Flow</b> (calculated, not a driver).</li>
<li>• Forecast objects should be <b>disclosed regularly</b> (transparency) — not necessarily individual/discrete.</li>
<li>• Abnormal growth <b>converges</b> back to the historical average.</li>
<li>• Maintenance capex ≈ depreciation; growth capex from management.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>

<section id="calculators" class="section-anchor mb-12">
<div class="section-head flex items-center gap-3 mb-5">
<div class="w-11 h-11 rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-br from-violet-500/20 to-cyan-500/10 border border-violet-500/30 flex items-center justify-center"><span class="lucide">🧮</span></div>
<div>
<div class="text-[11px] uppercase tracking-widest text-violet-400 font-bold">Interactive Tools</div>
<h2 class="section-title text-white">Live Calculators</h2>
</div>
</div>

<div class="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-5">
<!-- Gordon Growth Calculator -->
<div class="glass p-6" data-xdata="{D1: 10, r: 12, g: 4}">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-3"><span class="lucide">📈</span><h3 class="sub-title">Gordon Growth Model</h3></div>
<div class="formula-box mb-4 text-sm"><span class="tex">P<sub>0</sub> = <span class="frac"><span>D<sub>1</sub></span><span>r - g</span></span></span></div>
<div class="space-y-3">
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Next Year's Dividend (D₁) — ₹</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="D1" step="0.01" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Required Rate of Return (r) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="r" step="0.1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Growth Rate (g) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="g" step="0.1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
</div>
<div data-xif="r > g">
<div class="calc-result mt-4">
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-400 font-bold uppercase mb-1">Intrinsic Value P₀</div>
<div class="text-3xl font-black text-white">₹<span data-xtext="(D1 / ((r-g)/100)).toFixed(2)"></span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1" data-xtext="`= ${D1} / (${r/100} - ${g/100}) = ${D1} / ${((r-g)/100).toFixed(3)}`"></div>
</div>
</div>
<div data-xif="r <= g">
<div class="calc-result mt-4 !border-rose-500/40 !bg-rose-500/5">
<div class="text-xs text-rose-400 font-bold uppercase mb-1">⚠ INVALID</div>
<div class="text-sm text-rose-300">r must be &gt; g for Gordon Growth to work!</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Margin Call Calculator -->
<div class="glass p-6" data-xdata="{P0: 100, IM: 40, MM: 25}">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-3"><span class="lucide">🛑</span><h3 class="sub-title">Margin Call Price Calculator</h3></div>
<div class="formula-box mb-4 text-sm"><span class="tex">P<sup>*</sup> = <span class="frac"><span>P<sub>0</sub>(1-IM)</span><span>1-MM</span></span></span></div>
<div class="space-y-3">
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Initial Stock Price (P₀) — ₹</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="P0" step="0.5" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Initial Margin (IM) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="IM" step="1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Maintenance Margin (MM) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="MM" step="1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
</div>
<div class="calc-result mt-4">
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-400 font-bold uppercase mb-1">Margin Call Triggers At</div>
<div class="text-3xl font-black text-white">₹<span data-xtext="(P0 * (1 - IM/100) / (1 - MM/100)).toFixed(2)"></span></div>
<div class="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-2 space-y-0.5">
<div>Loan Amount: ₹<span data-xtext="(P0 * (1 - IM/100)).toFixed(2)"></span></div>
<div>Your Equity: ₹<span data-xtext="(P0 * IM/100).toFixed(2)"></span></div>
<div>Price decline before call: <span data-xtext="((1 - (P0 * (1 - IM/100) / (1 - MM/100)) / P0) * 100).toFixed(2)"></span>%</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Leverage & ROE Simulator -->
<div class="glass p-6" data-xdata="{asset: 100, equity: 60, assetReturn: 20}">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-3"><span class="lucide">•</span><h3 class="sub-title">Leverage & ROE Simulator</h3></div>
<div class="formula-box mb-4 text-sm"><span class="tex">ROE = Asset Return × <span class="frac"><span>Asset</span><span>Equity</span></span></span></div>
<div class="space-y-3">
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Total Asset Value — ₹</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="asset" step="1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Your Equity — ₹</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="equity" step="1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Asset Return — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="assetReturn" step="0.5" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
</div>
<div data-xif="equity > 0">
<div class="calc-result mt-4">
<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3">
<div>
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-400 font-bold uppercase mb-1">Leverage Ratio</div>
<div class="text-2xl font-black text-white" data-xtext="(asset/equity).toFixed(4)"></div>
</div>
<div>
<div class="text-xs text-cyan-400 font-bold uppercase mb-1">ROE</div>
<div class="text-2xl font-black" data-xclass="(assetReturn * asset/equity) >= 0 ? 'text-emerald-300' : 'text-rose-300'"><span data-xtext="(assetReturn * asset/equity).toFixed(2)"></span>%</div>
</div>
<div class="col-span-2 text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">
Debt: ₹<span data-xtext="(asset - equity).toFixed(2)"></span><br/>
For every ₹1 equity → control ₹<span data-xtext="(asset/equity).toFixed(4)"></span> of assets
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- Simple DCF / DDM 2-Year -->
<div class="glass p-6" data-xdata="{D0:1, g1:15, g2:5, r:11, n:2}">
<div class="flex items-center gap-2 mb-3"><span class="lucide">📈</span><h3 class="sub-title">Two-Stage DDM Calculator</h3></div>
<div class="formula-box mb-4 text-sm"><span class="tex">P<sub>0</sub> = Σ<sub>t=1</sub><sup>n</sup><span class="frac"><span>D<sub>t</sub></span><span>(1+r)<sup>t</sup></span></span> + <span class="frac"><span>P<sub>n</sub></span><span>(1+r)<sup>n</sup></span></span></span></div>
<div class="space-y-3">
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Recent Dividend (D₀) — ₹</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="D0" step="0.1" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2">
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">High Growth (g₁) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="g1" step="0.5" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Years of High Growth (n)</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="n" step="1" min="1" max="5" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
</div>
<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2">
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Stable Growth (g₂) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="g2" step="0.5" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
<div>
<label class="text-xs text-slate-400 font-semibold">Required Return (r) — %</label>
<input type="number" data-xmodel="r" step="0.5" class="num-input mt-1" />
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div data-xif="r > g2">
<div class="calc-result mt-4">
<div class="text-xs text-emerald-400 font-bold uppercase mb-1">Intrinsic Value P₀</div>
<div class="text-3xl font-black text-white">₹<span data-xtext="(() => {
